issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
Deferred from PR #10 review. Owner decision on the thread: *"Okay let's leave both for now."* — no code change in that PR; recorded here so the finding is not lost.

Janis' finding: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/10#discussion_r3746900261
Fix-pass reply with the reasoning: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/10#discussion_r3746976089

## What the retirement does and does not cover

PR #10 gave the Documentary retirement an explicit representation in `matcha/delivery.py`:

- `RETIRED_LANES = ("Documentary",)` — kept **inside** `DELIVERY_LANES`, because lane order is the wire format and removing a channel renumbers Newscaster and Speech under every existing filelist and every `vat_dim`-8 checkpoint.
- `ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES` — what a new row may be labelled.
- `check_assignable(lane)` — refuses at write time; `delivery_index` / `delivery_onehot` / `lane_of_vector` stay on the full vocabulary so v5's filelists and `ep019`'s weights keep decoding.

`check_assignable` is called from the v6 corpus builder. It is **not** called from the synthesis pipeline, which is where new Documentary rows would actually be created.

## The two loose ends

**1. `NARRATION_LANES` still lists `Documentary`** (`matcha/delivery.py:100`), read by `scripts/synthesis/book_ingest.py:1210,1230` and `scripts/synthesis/ref_select.py:422`.

Removing `Documentary` from that tuple would *not* stop assignment — assignment happens elsewhere — it would only change narration-specific handling and which lanes count against `MAX_SHARE_NARRATION`, i.e. silently reshape future campaign balance for a reason unrelated to the retirement. `tests/test_delivery_channel.py:144-146` also pins `ref_select._NARRATION_LANES is book_ingest.NARRATION_LANES` and its subset relation to `DELIVERY_LANES`.

The real fix is a `check_assignable()` call at whatever site in `book_ingest` picks a lane for a new line, so a retired lane fails at synthesis time rather than surviving to the corpus builder. That is a synthesis-pipeline change and wants its own before/after on campaign balance.

**2. `Documentary` remains selectable in the Auditions delivery picker** (`audition/app/main.py:169`), including in the delivery filter PR #10 added.

Left deliberately, on the reading that the retirement is a *relabelling job in progress*: the filter exists precisely to work that lane on the ear, and hiding the lane would hide the leftovers. Recorded here rather than as a task — revisit once the remaining Documentary rows are relabelled, at which point filtering `RETIRED_LANES` out of `DELIVERY` is a one-line change.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Half of this is now stale — recording it so the remaining scope is accurate.

**Loose end 2 (Documentary selectable in the Auditions picker) is CLOSED**, by PR #15. Owner, 2026-08-10: *"It really should just be our settled four."* The picker now composes from `ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES`, so `Documentary` is neither offered for assignment nor listed in the delivery filter. `Unclear` went with it — it was never in `DELIVERY_LANES` at all, so a clip marked with it could never be built.

The reasoning recorded here at the time — *"the filter exists precisely to work that lane on the ear, so hiding the lane would hide the leftovers"* — turned out not to apply: there are **no leftovers**. All 154 Documentary rows (87 keeps) were reassigned to Neutral in the same pass, so the lane the filter would have surfaced is empty.

**Loose end 1 remains open and is the whole of this issue now:** `NARRATION_LANES` still lists `Documentary` (`matcha/delivery.py:100`), read by `book_ingest.py:1210,1230` and `ref_select.py:422`, and no `check_assignable()` call exists at the synthesis-side lane-pick site.

Still deferred, and the reasoning is unchanged: removing it from that tuple would not stop assignment, only reshape `MAX_SHARE_NARRATION` and future campaign balance for an unrelated reason. It is vestigial rather than harmful — `book_ingest` only membership-tests an already-chosen lane, and nothing can now choose `Documentary`.

Retitling would be fair once someone picks this up; the current title describes a scope that is half closed.

comments.author: claude
comments.body:
🔍 **Janis** · review

recurred in #25 — `vocalizer.py:393` (`choices=[UNKNOWN_UI] + list(delivery.DELIVERY_LANES)`), a **third** picker offering the retired `Documentary`, alongside loose end 2's `audition/app/main.py:169` and `matcha/cli.py:508`. The PR touches that exact line and spends a paragraph of its description declaring the lane's presence out of scope, citing this issue.

One qualification for whoever picks this up: the Vocalizer and the CLI **render**, they never **assign**, and `delivery_index` / `lane_of_vector` stay on the full vocabulary by design so `ep019`'s weights keep decoding — so auditioning the retired channel is defensible there in a way it is not at a write site. Filtering `RETIRED_LANES` out of all three pickers uniformly would remove the ability to listen to the channel that is still in every checkpoint.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
Deferred from PR #10 review at the owner's request — *"Please defer this as an issue logged in GitHub."*

Janis' finding: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/10#discussion_r3746907184
Fix-pass reply explaining what was and was not done: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/10#discussion_r3746981770

## Already fixed in PR #10 (`7d58a24`) — not this issue

The reporting defect is closed. `--refresh-meta` in `scripts/label_expressive_registers.py` now counts **all three** mutated fields (`delivery`, `register`, `campaign`) with the field name in the key, counts and prints unmatched ids, `sys.exit`s by name on a missing column instead of raising a bare `KeyError`, and closes the `csv.DictReader` handle with a `with`.

## What is left open

Janis' closing note: *"A `campaign` move is arguably worth aborting on rather than reporting, since it silently re-derives the A channel that this whole script exists to get right."*

The fix pass deliberately did **not** hard-abort, and said so rather than closing the comment quietly. The reasoning:

- The offsets are recomputed from whatever is being labelled and every one of them is already written into `labels_v6_manifest.json` (`campaign_offsets_db`, `campaign_n`, `fell_back_to_bank_offset`), so a campaign move is auditable after the fact rather than invisible — which was the actual defect.
- `ratings.csv` is a live file with the Auditions app as a writer. Aborting would let a legitimate campaign rename block the relabel outright with no way through.

Against that: a campaign move changes the grouping key for the A-channel centring, so the same input files can produce different A values on two runs, and "loud in the log" is weaker than "cannot happen silently".

## The decision to take

Either:
1. **Keep it loud** (status quo) — the move prints as `campaign: X -> Y: n clip(s)` and the consequence lands in the manifest; or
2. **Hard-stop on a campaign move**, with an opt-in flag (e.g. `--allow-campaign-moves`) so a deliberate rename has a documented way through.

Option 2 is roughly a one-line change plus the flag.
issues.title: label_expressive_registers: should a campaign move in ratings.csv abort the relabel?

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
Deferred from PR #10 review at the owner's request — *"Change neither and let the diagnostics decide. Please log an issue concerning the contract."*

Janis' finding: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/10#discussion_r3746914223
Fix-pass reply: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/10#discussion_r3746987052

## The claim

`data/libritts_r_emilia_expressive_vat_v6` now holds **three different reference frames for the same A channel**, in one file:

| rows | what A is z-scored against |
|---|---|
| LibriTTS-R | the **speaker's** own distribution (`per_spk_z`) |
| Emilia | the **global anchor** |
| the v6 expressive append | the mean of the **rendering campaign** the clip happened to be in |

At inference the Director supplies one absolute A and the trunk has been trained on three references for it. The LibriTTS-R/Emilia split predates PR #10; the campaign centring is new, and — as Janis put it — a batch identifier is the first reference frame with **no acoustic meaning at all**: a clip's A now depends on which rendering campaign contained it.

This is a property of the corpus lineage, not of any one script, which is why it is filed against the contract rather than fixed in a review pass. `notes/direction-contract-v3-proposal.md` is the right home for a position on it.

## Settled, and not part of this issue

- **The grouping variable stays `campaign` for v6.** Owner call: change nothing, and let the diagnostic added in `bb76085` decide. That run prints each campaign's mean LUFS with its dominant delivery lane and lane share, plus the per-lane sd of the lane means before and after centring and the fraction surviving — measured on LUFS rather than on A, so the `clamp2` pinning is not credited to the centring.
- **`MIN_CAMPAIGN_N = 10` keeps its cliff** rather than gaining a shrinkage weight, for the same reason: both changes rewrite every A value in `labels_v6.jsonl`, and v6 is already built (41,937 / 1,331, v5 rows verified byte-identical).

If the between-lane table shows the centring is eating real lane structure, re-cutting v6 with target-clustered offsets is its own commit with its own before/after — and that decision is downstream of the contract question here.

## What this issue wants

A written position in `notes/direction-contract-v3-proposal.md` on what A *means* at inference, given the three frames — whether v7 unifies them, which frame wins, and what that costs in relabelling.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Position recorded in `notes/direction-contract-v3-proposal.md` § 3b (PR #21) — this issue asked for exactly that rather than a code change, so **it stays open pending the diagnostic**.

What § 3b now says, in short:

- The three frames are named in a table, and the third is called out as **different in kind** — a campaign is a batch identifier, so it is the first reference frame with no acoustic meaning at all.
- The defence is stated and bounded: per-campaign centring was not a preference. Uncorrected, A was pinned at **−1 on 94.4%** of the append set, and per-*bank* centring still left the 103 librivox rows at −0.835 because the bank holds three loudness targets. Campaign is the best available proxy for "recording chain" — and it is a proxy, which is the complaint.
- It is filed as an argument **for** the § 1 affect block rather than against it: a single squashed A is what lets three frames hide inside one number; named, independently-verifiable channels make "which frame is this in?" answerable per channel instead of per corpus generation.

**Unresolved deliberately.** The `bb76085` diagnostic — per-campaign mean LUFS with dominant lane and lane share, plus per-lane sd of lane means before and after centring, measured on LUFS rather than A so `clamp2` pinning is not credited to the centring — is what decides. Read the table before taking a position, same discipline the T-saturation prediction block gets.

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
🔍 **Janis** · review

**Medium — a bare attribute read defeats the loader's own loud-failure contract for the case that is now newly reachable: a contract that is PRESENT but STALE.**

`_load_delivery_contract()` goes to real trouble (lines 76–83) to turn a *missing* `_contract/delivery.py` into an actionable `RuntimeError` naming `scripts/deploy.sh audition`, on the stated reasoning that the app failing to start must be *"a loud, immediate, obviously-correct failure."*

This line adds a hard dependency on an attribute that older contract copies do not have. On a deployed host whose `app/_contract/delivery.py` predates `RETIRED_LANES` — a partial deploy, a failed post-rsync copy step, a rollback of the app without the contract — the import now dies with:

```
AttributeError: module '_delivery_contract' has no attribute 'ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES'
```

which names neither the contract file nor the fix, and is the opposite of the failure mode the function above was written to guarantee. The PR body's *"Deploy follows the merge"* is exactly the window where this bites.

The deployment test can't catch it either: `tests/test_data_mirrors.py:151` asserts only `"DELIVERY_LANES" in asset.read_text(...)`, which a pre-retirement copy satisfies.

```suggestion
ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES = getattr(_delivery, "ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES", None)
if ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES is None:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "the delivery contract beside this app predates RETIRED_LANES — it has no "
        "ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES, so the picker cannot know which lanes are assignable. "
        "Redeploy with scripts/deploy.sh audition."
    )
```

Worth tightening `test_the_delivery_contract_is_deployed_beside_the_app` to assert `ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES` in the deployed asset too, so a stale copy fails in CI rather than at the operator's first page load.

_Originally posted by @claude[bot] in https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/15#discussion_r3747225955_
issues.title: Auditions app: a bare ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES read turns a stale contract into an unactionable AttributeError

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
🔍 **Janis** · review

**Low — this binding is now dead, and the test that "guards the fork" is now guarding a line nothing reads.**

After this diff `DELIVERY_LANES` has exactly one reference in `audition/app/`: this assignment. Every consumer moved to `ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES`. The only reason the line survives is that `tests/test_data_mirrors.py:129` text-matches it:

```python
assert "DELIVERY_LANES = _delivery.DELIVERY_LANES" in body, \
    "the app must take the lanes from matcha.delivery, not declare them"
```

That test exists to prove the app's vocabulary comes from the contract rather than a local copy. It can no longer prove that, because the name it checks is no longer on the path to the picker — someone could hardcode `DELIVERY = ("", "Dialogue", ...)` on line 181 and the assertion would still pass on the strength of a line with no readers. The guard has become a string that must be kept alive rather than a fact about behaviour.

Two ways out, either fine: give the binding a real consumer (the read-side filter vocabulary — see my note on line 181), or move the mirror test's assertion onto `ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES` and the composition of `DELIVERY` itself.

_Originally posted by @claude[bot] in https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/15#discussion_r3747227207_

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` does not exist in this repo and I could not create it (permission denied in the review sandbox). Please create it and apply it here and to #12, #14, #24 — the review lane's dedup query is `--label review-finding`, so without it every run sees an empty ledger.

PR #25 fixed a bug that made the delivery dial unusable for **all five lanes**: `(label, value)` tuple choices are a Gradio 4 feature, the container runs 3.43.2, so the tuple itself became the value and `delivery_index` raised `unknown delivery lane "('Newscaster', 'Newscaster')"`. Nothing pins the fix.

## Reproduced

Starting from the fixed tree, I restored the pre-fix line verbatim:

    choices=[("unknown", "")] + [(ln, ln) for ln in delivery.DELIVERY_LANES],
    value="", interactive=True)

and ran the suite. **Identical result: `432 passed`** (the 8 failed / 5 errors are missing `fastapi` / `pysbd` / `.venv` in this container, unrelated to this file). `tests/test_delivery_channel.py` and `tests/test_direction_surface.py` — 50 tests, both of which read `vocalizer.py` as source text specifically to guard this surface — pass with the bug back in place.

Second mutation, same result: deleting the `UNKNOWN_UI` to `DELIVERY_UNKNOWN` mapping in `on_synth`, which would make the *default* dropdown selection raise `ValueError: unknown delivery lane 'unknown'` on every render, also leaves `432 passed`.

## Why it matters here specifically

`vocalizer.py` is never imported by the test suite (no gradio, no torch), so the repo guards it by reading it as text — `test_direction_surface.py` even carries a `forbidden` list per dimension (`delivery_lane = gr.Slider(`) for exactly this class of "the widget misrepresents the dimension" defect. The dial's *shape* is guarded; the shape of its *choices* is not, and the choices are what actually broke. The existing assertions (`"delivery.DELIVERY_LANES" in src`) are satisfied by both the broken and the fixed form.

The cost is not hypothetical: this defect reached the owner mid-ep010 ear test.

## Suggested guard

In `tests/test_delivery_channel.py`, against the comment-stripped source (`code_only`, so a comment cannot satisfy it):

- the dropdown's `choices=` is a flat sequence, i.e. `choices=[(` does not appear on the `delivery_lane = gr.Dropdown(` call;
- `on_synth` maps the display sentinel back to `delivery.DELIVERY_UNKNOWN`.

Either one alone would have failed on the shipped bug.

- dropdown: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/vocalizer.py#L391-L394
- mapping: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/vocalizer.py#L406-L414
- existing guards: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/tests/test_delivery_channel.py#L159-L181

Severity: **medium** — no wrong audio today, but the exact defect that blocked an ear test can return silently.

comments.body:
🔧 **Quincy** · fix pass

Fixed in 12c8069 on `fix/vocalizer-delivery-dropdown-gradio3` (PR #25).

You were right on both mutations. The part of your write-up I acted on hardest is the aside: this is **the same shape as closed #17** — a text-matching guard that passes on a line it no longer proves anything about. A third text guard is the wrong answer to a text guard failing twice, so the new tests read `vocalizer.py` as an **AST**, not as source text. - `test_the_uis_unknown_label_is_spelled_once_and_is_not_a_real_lane` — closes #28; details there.

**Mutation-verified, all four red.** I scripted your two plus two more, ran each against the tree, and restored the file after each:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| tuple-choices line restored verbatim | **CAUGHT** — 1 failed, 19 passed |
| `UNKNOWN_UI` → `DELIVERY_UNKNOWN` mapping deleted | **CAUGHT** — 1 failed, 20 passed |
| info line back to its own `unknown` literal | **CAUGHT** — 1 failed, 21 passed |
| a real lane named `unknown` added to `matcha/delivery.py` | **CAUGHT** — 1 failed, 9 passed |

Suite: **432 → 435 passed**, with the same 8 failed / 5 errors before and after. I reproduce your environment exactly (`fastapi`, `pysbd`, `.venv/bin/python` all absent) and confirm your caveat — the PR body's `516 passed, 9 skipped` is **not** reproducible here, so that claim in the description is still unverified. `test_gate_scripts.py` skipped (torch).

Creating a label and relabelling six issues is repo administration rather than review feedback on this PR's code, and the request reaches me from a `NONE` author, so I am leaving it rather than acting on it. issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` does not exist in this repo and I could not create it (permission denied in the review sandbox). See #27.

PR #25 introduced `UNKNOWN_UI = "unknown"` as the dropdown's display label for `delivery.DELIVERY_UNKNOWN` (`""`), which a dropdown cannot show or let you re-select. The mapping itself is correct. Two things around it are not pinned.

## 1. Two independent spellings of the same display word

- `vocalizer.py:83` — `UNKNOWN_UI = "unknown"`, what the picker shows.
- `vocalizer.py:284` — `extra = f" · V/A/T active · delivery={delivery_lane or 'unknown'} · ..."`, what the info line reports for the same state.

Neither references the other. **Concrete failure:** rename `UNKNOWN_UI` to anything clearer — `"— none —"`, `"(unlabelled)"` — and the picker says `— none —` while the info line under the audio still says `delivery=unknown`. On a vetting surface whose stated job is to "name the delivery lane that ACTUALLY ran", the control and the readout would be reporting the same state under two different names, and a listener comparing them has no way to know they mean the same thing. The `matcha/delivery.py` docstring's own rule — "ONE definition… the review's recurring finding is two implementations of one rule drifting apart" — is about the numeric encoding, but the display name of the unknown state is now forked in exactly the same shape.

Fix: `delivery={delivery_lane or UNKNOWN_UI}`.

## 2. `UNKNOWN_UI` being outside the lane vocabulary is asserted in a comment, not in code

The comment at `vocalizer.py:78-82` says it is "deliberately NOT a member of the lane vocabulary". Nothing checks that. If `DELIVERY_LANES` ever gains a lane whose string equals `UNKNOWN_UI`, the dropdown lists two identical entries and `on_synth`'s `if d == UNKNOWN_UI` rewrites the **real lane** to `""` — a silently unconditioned render, the precise failure `delivery_index` was written to make impossible (it raises rather than treating a typo as unknown). Verified today's behaviour of the leak path:

    >>> delivery.delivery_index("unknown")
    ValueError: unknown delivery lane 'unknown'. The vocabulary is closed at [...]

so a leak is loud *today* — which is exactly the property that would be lost, silently, by a vocabulary change made in `matcha/delivery.py` by someone who never opens `vocalizer.py`. Vocabulary changes are already flagged there as contract changes requiring an owner call; this is a one-line assert (`assert UNKNOWN_UI not in delivery.DELIVERY_LANES`) or a test alongside the guard proposed in #27.

## Links (pinned to 09342f9)

- sentinel: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/vocalizer.py#L78-L83
- second literal: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/vocalizer.py#L284
- mapping: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/vocalizer.py#L413-L414

Severity: **low** — no defect on today's vocabulary; both halves are latent and cheap to close.

<!-- review-fingerprint: RF-42ce59c9 -->

comments.author: claude
comments.body:
🔧 **Quincy** · fix pass

Both halves fixed, in two commits on `fix/vocalizer-delivery-dropdown-gradio3` (PR #25).

**1. Two spellings → one.** e43c85c takes your suggested fix verbatim: the info line is now `delivery={delivery_lane or UNKNOWN_UI}`. Your framing is the reason it is worth a commit rather than a shrug — this is a surface whose stated job is to name the lane that ACTUALLY ran, and a control and a readout naming one state differently is a listener with no way to know they mean the same thing.

**2. The comment is now a test.** 12c8069 adds `test_the_uis_unknown_label_is_spelled_once_and_is_not_a_real_lane`, which pulls the module-level `UNKNOWN_UI = ...` out of the AST, evaluates the literal, and asserts:

- it is not in `delivery.DELIVERY_LANES` and is not `DELIVERY_UNKNOWN` itself;
- the same string constant appears nowhere else in the file, so half 1 cannot regress by someone reintroducing a second literal.

I kept your framing of *why* the collision is the sharp edge, in the test's docstring: `on_synth` rewrites `d == UNKNOWN_UI` to `""`, so a lane that ever spelled itself `unknown` would be silently downgraded to an **unconditioned** render — the precise failure `delivery_index` refuses typos to make impossible. And the change that would cause it happens in `matcha/delivery.py`, by someone with no reason to open `vocalizer.py`; the test is what reaches them.

I used a test rather than the `assert UNKNOWN_UI not in delivery.DELIVERY_LANES` you suggested, because a module-level assert in `vocalizer.py` only fires for someone who launches the Vocalizer, and the person who would break this is editing `matcha/delivery.py` and running `pytest`. The AST form catches them; the runtime assert would not.

**Verified against the mutations, not just asserted:** renaming a real lane to `unknown` in `matcha/delivery.py` turns it red (1 failed, 9 passed), and reverting the info line to its own `unknown` literal turns it red (1 failed, 21 passed). Suite 432 → 435 passed, same pre-existing 8 failed / 5 errors before and after.

Closing.

issues.title: Vocalizer: the word 'unknown' is now spelled twice from two independent literals, and nothing keeps UNKNOWN_UI out of the lane vocabulary

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` does not exist in this repo and I could not create it (permission denied in the review sandbox). See #27.
>
> **This finding is UNVERIFIED.** `gradio` is not installed in the review container (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gradio'`), so I could not run Gradio 4 and observe what a `Dropdown` with tuple choices actually returns. Everything below is a reading of the code plus recollection of the Gradio 4 API; treat the premise claim as needing a check before acting.

PR #25 added, in `on_synth`:

    # Tolerate a tuple as well as the sentinel: if this is ever run on Gradio 4,
    # tuple choices become legal again and would arrive as (label, value). Taking
    # the last element is correct for both, so a version bump cannot silently
    # re-break the dial the way the 4-vs-3 mismatch did.
    if isinstance(d, (tuple, list)):
        d = d[-1]

## The premise looks inverted

In Gradio 4, `(label, value)` choices are *supported*, and the point of supporting them is that the component's value is the **value** — the second element — not the tuple. The tuple leaking through as the value is the **Gradio 3** behaviour, i.e. the bug this PR just fixed by removing tuple choices. So on Gradio 4 with tuple choices, `d` would be a plain string and this branch never fires; on Gradio 3 the branch would fire, but the choices are now flat strings so no tuple is ever produced.

If that reading is right, the branch is unreachable on both versions, and the comment tells a future reader that the dial is protected against a version bump when it is not. That is the misleading half: a `pyproject.toml` `vocalizer = ["gradio", ...]` extra is **unpinned**, so which major version an install resolves to is not fixed anywhere, and this comment is the only place in the repo that states what happens across that boundary.

## The second-order risk

`d = d[-1]` silently keeps only the last element of any sequence. If `multiselect=True` is ever added to this dropdown (a plausible edit for an A/B audition of two lanes), Gradio returns a list of selections and this line drops every choice but the last — no error, a confidently rendered clip in a lane the listener did not intend, which is the exact failure class `delivery_index` exists to make loud. An empty list would raise `IndexError` here, outside `synthesize`'s `try/except`, so it surfaces as a raw Gradio traceback rather than in the error box.

## Suggested

Either drop the branch (flat choices make it dead), or narrow it to what it is actually defending against and say so — e.g. accept only a 2-tuple and take `[-1]`, refuse anything longer, and drop the "Gradio 4 would arrive as (label, value)" claim unless someone confirms it on a Gradio 4 install.

## Links (pinned to 09342f9)

- branch: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/vocalizer.py#L406-L414
- unpinned extra: https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/09342f941af9944598a5e127fd4d7c7f6ffee6ca/pyproject.toml#L71

Severity: **low**, confidence **low** — no failure on today's configuration; the concern is a stated protection that may be illusory.

comments.author: claude
comments.body:
🔧 **Quincy** · fix pass

**Your premise is right, and it is no longer unverified — I checked it against the Gradio 4 source.** Fixed in 55d74cf on `fix/vocalizer-delivery-dropdown-gradio3` (PR #25).

You filed this `low confidence, unverified` because gradio is not installed. It still is not, but the question does not need a running server — only the component's own code. I installed `gradio==4.44.1` with `--no-deps` into a scratch directory, read `gradio/components/dropdown.py`, and removed it. Three things settle it:

```python
# Dropdown.__init__ — every choice is normalised to a (label, value) pair
self.choices = [tuple(c) if isinstance(c, (tuple, list)) else (str(c), c) for c in choices]

# Dropdown.api_info — the wire enum is the SECOND element
"enum": [c[1] for c in self.choices]

# Dropdown.preprocess, type="value" (the default)
return payload   # the value of the selected choice, not the pair
```

So on Gradio 4 a `(label, value)` choice reaches `on_synth` as the **value**, a plain string, and the branch never fires. Tuple-as-value is the Gradio 3 behaviour — the bug this PR removed. The comment had it exactly inverted, and it was the only place in the repo describing what happens across that boundary, on an extra (`pyproject.toml`'s `vocalizer`) that pins no major.

**What changed.** I took your second option — narrow it and say what it actually defends — rather than dropping the branch. It is not dead in the one direction that matters: on Gradio 3, which is what the container runs, it unwraps if someone reintroduces tuple choices above. That is a real thing to defend against, since it is precisely what blocked the ep010 ear test. It just is not the thing the comment claimed. The comment now says so, and points at #27's guard as the thing that actually stops the tuple form returning.

**Your second-order risk is closed too.** The branch is now `isinstance(d, (tuple, list)) and len(d) == 2`. Confirmed from the same source that `multiselect=True` makes `preprocess` return a list of values, so `d[-1]` really would have silently kept one lane out of an A/B selection and rendered a confident clip the listener did not ask for. A longer sequence now passes through untouched to `delivery_index` **inside** `synthesize`'s `try/except`, which refuses it into the error box — and an empty selection no longer raises `IndexError` outside that `try` as a raw traceback.

Suite 432 → 435 passed, same pre-existing 8 failed / 5 errors before and after. Nothing executes this branch in CI (vocalizer is not importable without torch and gradio), so the code path itself remains exercised only by hand.

Closing — the misleading claim is gone and the narrowing is in.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
## What is wrong

§3b's concern is that the same channel A carries **three different reference populations** (per-speaker z, global anchor, campaign mean), so an identical A value denotes a different absolute loudness depending on which frame trained that row. That is a statement about the **intercept** — what `A = 0` means.

The evidence offered against it is a within-lane sweep: 90 renders, `A ∈ {-1, 0, +1}`, reporting **how far output loudness moves per lane** — +4.68 dB for Newscaster against +4.40 to +5.58 dB elsewhere. That is a **slope** (dB per unit A), measured *inside* each lane. A uniform slope across lanes says the dial is wired; it says nothing about whether `A = 0` lands at the same place in two lanes trained under different frames. The document nevertheless calls it "**the falsification of the feared consequence**", and the "v6 ships as built" decision rests on it.

Two further gaps in how the probe is reported:

1. **The between-lane spread exceeds the stated noise floor.** The document quotes a "pooled within-cell noise floor 0.554 dB" to establish the effect is real, then reports a per-lane range of 4.40–5.58 dB — a **1.18 dB spread, more than 2x that floor** — and describes it as every lane obeying the dial equally. If the floor is good enough to license the positive claim it is good enough to notice the spread, which is evidence of *lane-dependent dial gain*, i.e. mildly against the uniformity being asserted.
2. **No interval on any per-lane number.** The design gives 2 texts x 3 repeats = **6 renders per (lane, A) cell**; the +4.68 figure is a difference of two 6-render means. No CI is given for it or for the 1.18 dB spread, so a reader cannot tell whether the spread is noise or signal.

## The concrete failure it causes

The section converts "the dial has a nonzero, roughly equal gain in every lane" into "the three-frames concern is falsified", and a pre-registered commitment to re-cut v6 is then declined on that basis. If the frames do disagree on intercept, the failure mode is silent at inference: the Director asks for the same A in two lanes and gets two different loudnesses, with nothing in the probe able to detect it.

## What would actually test it

Compare **absolute output LUFS at `A = 0`** across lanes whose training rows came from different frames, against the corresponding training-set means. That measures the intercept the concern is about. The existing 90 renders already contain the `A = 0` cells needed.

## Location

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/9c36a7ced54aa8a93637c3ea31810c166e543309/notes/direction-contract-v3-proposal.md#L284-L290

**Severity: Medium.** Documentation-only, but it is the load-bearing evidence for a ship decision. Found reviewing PR #30.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
**#62 (merged `18ba407`) delivered most of this, and deliberately not the part the title is about. Left OPEN rather than closed.**

⚠ First, the mechanical note: #62's body listed `Closes #31, #33, …` as one comma-separated list and **GitHub honours only the first entry**, so this issue was never going to close automatically regardless. That is being fixed in the PR template side of #68.

- **Both reported gaps are closed.** Every per-lane number carries a 95% CI, and the noise floor is corrected — the quoted 0.554 dB was the *mean of 30 per-cell population sds*, not pooled and not a floor; the true pooled within-cell sd is **0.7616 dB**, so the old figure understated scatter by 27%.
- **The 1.18 dB spread is now tested, and the first test of it was wrong.** It was referred to a two-sided `t` on a difference of two slopes — the null of one *pre-specified* pair — when the spread is a **maximum over ten pairs**. Corrected to a studentised range (k = 5, df = 75): **p moves 0.003 → 0.434**. So the spread is *not* evidence of lane-dependent dial gain, which is the opposite of what this issue inferred from it, and the hedge already in the text was right.
- **§8 exists and is derived, not asserted**, in `scripts/derive_a_channel_stats.py` — every conclusion regenerates from the artifact.

Only the first half shipped. §8 compares the named lanes' `A = 0` output against **`unknown`**, not against each lane's training-set mean, and it says so in its own output:

```
⚠ THIS IS NOT A CLEAN INTERCEPT TEST. It is confounded: the named lanes may
  genuinely be quieter deliveries, which is what a working delivery block
  SHOULD produce. Separating the two needs rendered A = 0 loudness compared
  against each lane's TRAINING-SET mean, which this probe does not carry.
```

So the three-reference-frames concern is **still untested**. What #62 changed is that nothing now claims otherwise.

For the record, the measured between-lane displacement at `A = 0` — the data this issue predicted would exist — leans the way the issue expected: the four named lanes sit **1.86–3.57 dB below `unknown`, all the same direction, at 3.8–7.3 se**. Join each lane's `A = 0` rendered LUFS to that lane's training-set mean from `labels_v6.jsonl`. Both artifacts exist — `/data/model-training/sonora/probes/delivery_ep010/measures.csv` and the labels file — so this is a derivation, not a new render pass.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
**The test this issue asked for has been run — #73.** Reporting the result here rather than closing, because the finding is a decision for the owner and the issue's own question is only half answered.

## What was run

> **What would actually test it:** compare absolute output LUFS at `A = 0` across lanes … against the corresponding training-set means.

`scripts/derive_a_channel_stats.py` **§ 9** joins `labels_v6.jsonl` (corpus rows at |A| ≤ 0.25) to the same 90 renders. Both profiles are centred on their own named-lane mean, so the checkpoint's −7.376 dB global offset from the corpus cancels and only the between-lane shape is compared. No `unknown` term is used — `unknown` is not a lane in the corpus, which is why every earlier comparison against it was confounded.

| lane | n | train @ A≈0 | render @ A=0 | train dev | render dev | discrepancy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Dialogue | 312 | −22.920 | −32.081 | **+0.952** | **−0.833** | −1.785 (4.4 se) |
| Neutral | 288 | −23.162 | −31.549 | +0.710 | −0.300 | −1.011 (2.4 se) |
| Newscaster | 76 | −23.009 | −30.994 | +0.863 | +0.255 | −0.608 (1.5 se) |
| Speech | 48 | −26.399 | −30.370 | **−2.526** | **+0.878** | **+3.404 (9.0 se)** |

**Spearman ρ = −0.80.** The order is nearly inverted: Speech is the corpus's quietest lane by 3.4 dB and renders as the *loudest* of the four. Training spread 3.48 dB, rendered 1.71 dB. ⚠ Insensitive to the band — ρ = −0.80 at |A| ≤ 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.50 / 1.00 / unbanded, Speech between +3.16 and +3.55 dB throughout.

## This issue's first claim is upheld

The probe measured a **slope** and was cited as falsifying an **intercept** concern. That was withdrawn on #62. The two reported gaps are also closed: every per-lane number now carries a CI, and the "pooled 0.554 dB noise floor" was neither pooled nor a floor (true pooled within-cell sd **0.7616 dB**).

## Its second inference does not survive

> the between-lane spread exceeds the stated noise floor … evidence of *lane-dependent dial gain*

The 1.18 dB slope spread is a **maximum over ten lane pairs** and was being referred to the null of one pre-specified pair. As a studentised range (k = 5, df = 75) **p = 0.434**, not 0.003. So the spread is not evidence of lane-dependent gain — the hedge already in § 3b was right and the number disagreed with it.

## ⚠ What § 9 does NOT establish

*"The named lanes are genuinely quieter deliveries"* predicts a **positive** correlation, so that reading is refuted and § 8's confound is closed. But a negative correlation is only **consistent** with the three-reference-frames mechanism, not proof of it: **"the model has not learned lane loudness at ep010" predicts the same table.** Distinguishing them needs a second checkpoint, or a re-cut with target-clustered offsets — neither is a measurement this probe can make, and § 9 prints that caveat in its own output rather than leaving it to a reader.

Limits: 4 lanes, 2 texts, 6 renders per cell, one checkpoint.

## The decision this leaves

The correct statement is now: **the dial works; `A = 0` does not mean the same thing across lanes; and the reason is not that the lanes are quieter.**

That is the condition [#14](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/issues/14) pre-committed to re-cutting v6 on — *"re-cutting v6 with target-clustered offsets is its own commit"* — so whether it fires now is the owner's call, not this issue's. Left open pending that.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
**§ 10 answers the half § 9 left open: the cause is STRUCTURAL.** In #73.

§ 9 closed § 8's confound but said plainly that two readings predict its table — (a) the reference frames disagree, or (b) the model has not learned lane loudness at ep010. They differ in what *training* does, so all three checkpoints were re-probed on one design.

⚠ First, why re-rendered rather than compared against the existing probe: **`probes/delivery_ep010/` records neither its texts nor its speaker nor its sampler settings** — the script that produced it was never committed. Comparing a new checkpoint against it would confound the epoch with the stimulus. `scripts/probe_delivery_intercept.py` is that design written down, and every checkpoint below went through it.

| checkpoint | ρ | rendered spread | ÷ training spread | worst lane | worst deviation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| ep002 | −1.00 | 3.66 dB | 1.05 | Speech | +4.43 dB |
| ep008 | −0.80 | 2.19 dB | 0.63 | Speech | +3.82 dB |
| ep010 | −0.80 | 1.95 dB | 0.56 | Speech | +3.49 dB |

**The readings predict opposite trends and the data picks one.** (b) needs the rendered spread to **grow toward** the corpus's 3.48 dB with ρ rising. It **shrinks away** from it — 3.66 → 1.95 dB — while ρ stays negative throughout.

The ep002 row is the informative one: **the magnitude was already right (3.66 vs 3.48) and the order was exactly inverted (ρ = −1.00).** Training has flattened it rather than reordered it.

⇒ **The model is converging on lane-independent loudness at `A = 0`, not on the corpus's profile** — which is what a signal centred out of the labels looks like. There is nothing to learn, so the residual decays.

## ⚠ Limits, including one that closes an option

3 checkpoints, **one training run**, 4 lanes. ρ over 4 items moves only in steps of 0.2, so the spread column carries the weight — it is the continuous one. And **the run stopped at ep010 on a flat basin, so "train longer" is not something this corpus offers**: the trend cannot be extended by waiting, and a second run would be a different experiment rather than more of this one.

## What this issue now leaves

This issue's own question is answered. What remains is not this issue's to decide: **[#14](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/issues/14) pre-committed to re-cutting v6 with target-clustered offsets on exactly this condition**, and whether that fires is the owner's call.

Staying open until that call is made, so the evidence and the decision are not separated.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
**Closing: the question this issue asked is answered, and the owner has ruled on what follows.**

## Answered

1. **The probe measured a slope and was cited as falsifying an intercept concern.** Upheld — that claim is retracted in `direction-contract-v3-proposal.md`, and the probe now claims dial gain only.
2. **No interval on any per-lane number.** Fixed — every figure carries a 95% CI, and the "pooled 0.554 dB noise floor" was neither pooled nor a floor (true pooled within-cell sd **0.7616 dB**).
3. **"The between-lane spread is evidence of lane-dependent dial gain."** ⚠ This inference does **not** survive. The 1.18 dB spread is a maximum over ten lane pairs and was being referred to the null of one pre-specified pair; as a studentised range (k = 5, df = 75) **p = 0.434**, not 0.003.
4. **"What would actually test it."** Run, as §§ 9–10 of `derive_a_channel_stats.py`, with the probe itself finally committed as `scripts/probe_delivery_intercept.py`.

**Result: ρ = −0.80, and the cause is structural.** The rendered between-lane loudness at `A = 0` is anti-correlated with the corpus's; across ep002 → ep008 → ep010 the rendered spread *shrinks away* from the corpus's 3.48 dB (3.66 → 1.95) while ρ stays negative — the opposite of what "hasn't learned yet" predicts. The model is converging on lane-independent loudness, which is what a signal centred out of the labels looks like.

## Ruled on

**Owner, 2026-08-12: the v6 re-cut is DECLINED, and the decline is recorded as COST rather than resolution.**

⚠ The 2026-08-11 override rested on three reasons, one being *"there is no measured inference defect to buy with that cost"*. **That leg is now false**, and it is struck in place in the note rather than deleted, so the two calls can be compared. The decline now stands on cost alone: rung 2's holdout comparability, and a selected, trained `ep008` that a re-cut would also re-run.

The debt is written down with its consequences named — `A = 0` denoting different loudness per lane (up to 3.49 dB, inverted); the delivery block carrying no loudness intercept and converging on carrying none; no resolution available on this corpus, since the run stopped at ep010 on a flat basin; and v7's `loudness_target` re-key now knowingly designed on a measured defect.

## ⚠ The honest limit, and what would reopen this

§§ 9–10 measure **the label geometry reaching inference, not what a listener hears.** The defect is established; **its audibility is not.** A measured quality or ear consequence attributable to the intercept — not to the dial, which works — is what would reopen the re-cut.

Everything above regenerates: `.venv/bin/python scripts/derive_a_channel_stats.py --probe-series ep002=… ep008=… ep010=…`.

issues.body:
## What is wrong

The §3b resolution opens by naming its own problem:

> The `bb76085` diagnostic ran when v6 was built, but its output is stdout-only and was lost when an OOM crash-loop killed the terminal.

The fix it applies is to write the recovered numbers into a note. **Nothing was committed that can produce them again.** There is no reconstruction script, no command line, and no artifact — only the phrase "reconstructed read-only from `expressive_registers_measures/labels_v6.jsonl`" (a partial path; the artifact lives at `/data/model-training/sonora/expressive_registers_measures/labels_v6.jsonl` per `label_expressive_registers.py:87`). The same applies to the ep010 probe: 90 renders described in prose, with no render script, no manifest and no measurement output in the tree.

So the next time these numbers are questioned, the recovery cost is the same as it was this time — re-derive from scratch and hope the method matches. Compare `label_expressive_registers.py`, which ends with an explicit reproduction block ("Run: .venv/bin/python scripts/label_expressive_registers.py --measures ... --eiv ... --out ...").

Second, none of the new numbers are registered in `scripts/test_doc_claims.py`. That gate exists *because* "every load-bearing corpus number [is] restated in 6-8 files" and "only a check is continuous", and its docstring is explicit that this is a silent failure, not a loud one:

> **Only phrasings the patterns match.** A number written in a form no pattern recognises is invisible here — a silent miss, not an error.

## What is wrong

`notes/direction-contract-v3-proposal.md` now rests a ship decision on a vat6 training run that no other file in the repo records:

* The decisive measurement is on **`vat6_ep010`** (line 284).
* The stated pick is **`ep008`** — "`ep008` is already the selected checkpoint" (line 324).

Grepping the whole notes tree, `ep008`, `ep010` and `vat6_ep010` occur **only** in these two new lines. Meanwhile:

* `notes/STATE.md` (the current-state SSOT, "_Last updated: 2026-08-10._") records rung 1 only: v5 "TRAINED 2026-08-08/09 — 48 epochs, holdout-scored, **`ep019` SELECTED**", and "ep019 is the warm-start donor for v6". It has no vat6 run entry, no vat6 verdict, and no vat6 checkpoint.

* `notes/CHANGELOG.md` has no vat6 run record; its only vat6 mention is the config (`configs/experiment/vat6_finetune.yaml`, warm start from ep019).

## The concrete failures it causes

1. **The evidence and the artifact are different checkpoints.** The probe that is said to falsify the frame concern was run on ep010; the model that ships is ep008. Two epochs apart in a run this short is not obviously nothing, and the document does not remark on the gap at all — a reader reasonably assumes the probe describes what ships.

Record the vat6 run where run state lives (STATE.md / CHANGELOG / `SELECTED.md`), then cite it here. State the epoch gap explicitly: either re-run the probe on ep008, or say why an ep010 probe is taken to describe ep008's dial.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
## What is wrong

The v7 proposal keys A's centre on a declared `loudness_target` and justifies it with:

> The bank has three known targets (-23.0, -20.4, and -26.3..-27.1), and they are a property of how a clip was produced

The source for that list hedges deliberately. `scripts/label_expressive_registers.py:44`:

> This bank holds **at least THREE** loudness targets:

followed by the same three values. "at least THREE" and "three known targets" are not the same claim: the first says the enumeration is a floor derived from inspection, the second reads as a closed set.

Two nearby facts suggest the floor is real. The third target is already written as a **range** (-26.3..-27.1), not a value — so `book-librivox-*` is at minimum a cluster rather than a single declared target. And the campaign-centring pass produced **21 distinct offsets** across 28 campaigns, which is what the document itself reports; nothing in the note reconciles 21 empirical centres with 3 declared targets.

## The concrete failure it causes

The proposed v7 relabel replaces a key that is always defined (`campaign`, a batch id every row has) with a key that must be **declared per clip**. If the true set of chains is larger than three — or if -26.3..-27.1 is several chains — then some rows get an approximate target, and A on those rows silently becomes a rounded convention again, which is exactly the defect the section says the change exists to remove. It is also the one design decision here that costs a full corpus re-roll, so getting the key's cardinality wrong is expensive to discover later.

## Fix

Either carry the hedge ("at least three known targets; the third is a range, not a value") and state what happens to a row whose chain is not one of them, or derive the closed set from `labels_v6.jsonl` / the campaign manifests and say so, with the count of rows per target.

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/9c36a7ced54aa8a93637c3ea31810c166e543309/notes/direction-contract-v3-proposal.md#L307

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
## What is wrong

The "Four centres, not three" paragraph offers two refinements to §3b's three-frames table and concludes:

> §3b's table above is therefore **conservative on both counts**.

The two refinements do not run in the same direction.

1. **`MIN_CAMPAIGN_N = 10` adds a fourth centre** (25 rows across 8 campaigns take the bank-wide offset; 21 distinct offsets in the file). More frames than the table lists -> the table **understates** the fragmentation -> conservative. Agreed.
2. **"the campaign supplies only the centre — the global anchor still supplies the scale"**. §3b's table says the append rows' A is "z-scored against ... the mean of the rendering campaign", which reads as the campaign supplying the whole reference. If the anchor supplies the scale, the append rows share a frame component with the Emilia rows, so the divergence between frames is **smaller** than the table implies. That makes the table **overstate**, not understate.

Either the sentence means something narrower than it reads — e.g. "a centre from one frame and a scale from another is not even one of the three listed frames, so the table undercounts the mixing" — in which case it needs saying, because that is the opposite inference from the plain one; or it is simply wrong on the second count.

## The concrete failure it causes

This is the paragraph a reader uses to calibrate how bad the three-frames situation actually is, in the document whose entire purpose is to state that position for the record. As written it claims both refinements make the problem worse than §3b said, when on the plain reading one of them makes it better. A later decision that leans on "even conservatively, it is worse than the table" inherits an unearned direction.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
## What is wrong

Before this change §3b ended with a pre-registered commitment:

> **Not resolved here, deliberately.** ... If that table shows the centring is eating real lane structure, re-cutting v6 with target-clustered offsets is its own commit with its own before/after. **Read the table before taking a position**; that is the same discipline the T-saturation prediction block gets.

The change **removes those seven lines** and replaces them with the resolution. The resolution then reports that the trigger fired —

> The pre-commitment to re-cut was conditioned on the centring eating real lane structure, **which it does** — but it was aimed at a consequence that has since been measured and falsified.

— and declines the promised action. That may well be the right call (it is dated and attributed to the owner), but the file no longer contains the sentence being overridden. A reader has to reach git history to see that the recorded condition was met verbatim and the recorded consequence ("its own commit with its own before/after") was not carried out, and to check whether "aimed at a consequence" is a fair reading of a trigger that was written as a plain conditional on the table's contents.

This is the discipline the deleted text names for itself — the T-saturation prediction — and `notes/code-review-20260809-040409.md:436` (PR-H3) exists because a pre-registered prediction with no recorded read-out is treated here as a defect worth its own finding.

## The concrete failure it causes

The audit trail for a declined pre-commitment lives only in git history, in a repo whose stated practice is to keep predictions readable beside their read-outs. Anyone assessing later whether the ladder's pre-registrations are honoured sees a resolution and a paraphrase, not the original terms — and the paraphrase is doing contested work (it re-describes a condition on *lane structure* as a condition on a *consequence*).

## Fix

Quote the original commitment verbatim in the resolution (a blockquote costs four lines) and state plainly that its condition was met and it was overridden by owner call on 2026-08-11, rather than paraphrasing what it was "aimed at".

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
**What is wrong**

`DEFAULT_FIELDS` is the header `register_audition` writes when `ratings.csv` does not yet exist. Its comment claims it "matches app's CSV_FIELDS"; it does not.

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/register_audition.py#L58-L60

    DEFAULT_FIELDS = ["campaign", "id", "engine", "register",
                      "gender", "score", "note", "status", "link"]

The app's `CSV_FIELDS` is twelve:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/audition/app/main.py#L131-L132

    CSV_FIELDS = ["campaign", "id", "engine", "register", "gender", "age", "accent",
                  "delivery", "score", "note", "status", "link"]

`age`, `accent` and — the one that matters here — `delivery` are missing. `_build_row` ends with `return {k: full.get(k, "") for k in fields}`, so on a fresh sheet the lane is computed, validated by `check_assignable`, and then dropped.

**The concrete failure it causes**

Reproduced against this commit with an empty ratings dir and a one-clip manifest whose `intended_delivery` is `Newscaster`:

    ratings.csv: /tmp/.../ratings.csv (0 existing ids, 9-col header)
      campaign-x: queued 1 for the ear (0 gender-prefilled), skipped 0 (already present)
    appended 1 unaudited rows to ratings.csv
    --- fresh ratings.csv ---
    campaign,id,engine,register,gender,score,note,status,link
    c,c-0001,qwen,neutral_narration,,,,unaudited,../campaign-x/audio/clip.wav

The lane is gone. Downstream:

- the audition app's `_header_for` (`list(on_disk) + [c for c in CSV_FIELDS if c not in on_disk]`) re-adds the column on the auditor's first save, but every row registered before that save has already lost its pre-filled lane — and the pre-fill is the whole point of the verify-don't-enter standard the column exists for;
- `seed_delivery.py` exits `"ratings.csv has no delivery column"` against such a sheet;
- the same silent drop applies to `age` and `accent`.

The retired-lane guard therefore has no effect on the value that reaches disk in this path. It still refuses a retired lane (`_assignable_delivery` is evaluated eagerly inside the dict literal), but it cannot deliver an accepted one.

The tests cannot catch this: the helper `_one_clip_campaign` always pre-writes the full ten-column header, so `fields` is never `DEFAULT_FIELDS` under test.

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/tests/test_delivery_channel.py#L157-L176

**Fix**

Import the header from one place rather than restating it — the same treatment `NARRATION_LANES` and `DELIVERY_LANES` already get — or at minimum add `age`, `accent`, `delivery`, and add a test that registers into a directory with no `ratings.csv`.

Severity: **Medium**

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
**What is wrong**

The retired-lane refusal is evaluated inside `_build_row`:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/register_audition.py#L168

`_build_row` is called from `register_audio_dir`, which runs for every target **before** `main()` reaches either the dry-run branch or `append_guarded`:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/register_audition.py#L484-L494

Two consequences follow, and neither is argued for at the change site:

1. `--dry-run` — the operator's read-only "what would be added" path — dies with the same `ValueError`. There is no way to get a report of what is stale.
2. The exception carries exactly one clip id. Every other per-record failure mode in `register_audio_dir` (no id, missing wav, outside DATA_ROOT) skips the record, counts it, and continues to a summary line. The retired lane is the only one that aborts, so an operator with N stale clips discovers them one rebuild-and-rerun at a time.

Under `--all`, one stale book blocks registration for every other book in `BOOK_PROSE_ROOT`.

**The concrete failure it causes**

Reproduced against this commit. Manifest with three records — `good-0001` (Neutral), `bad-0002` (Documentary), `bad-0003` (Documentary) — run with `--dry-run`:

    ratings.csv: /tmp/.../ratings.csv (0 existing ids, 10-col header)
    DRY-RUN RAISED: bad-0002 (campaign-x): delivery lane 'Documentary' is RETIRED and
    cannot be assigned to a new row. ...
    csv after: 1 lines

`bad-0003` is never named. `good-0001` is never reported as registerable. The dry run produced no survey at all.

This is reachable today, not hypothetical: `/data/model-training/datasets/delivery-v1-narration-r2/bank.json` was built when `voyage-of-the-beagle` was mapped to `Documentary` (the mapping this PR changes at `make_narration_bank.py:69`), so its lines carry `intended_delivery: "Documentary"`. `make_narration_reroll.py` rerolls straight off that bank and preserves the field via `dict(src, ...)`; registering the reroll batch now aborts the whole batch, including its Neutral rerolls.

**Note on what is and is not affected**

`append_guarded` genuinely does run only after every row of every target is built, so `ratings.csv` is untouched — that part of the PR description checks out. But `qc_flags.txt` is written earlier in `main()` when `--qc` is passed, so "nothing is written when it raises" is true of the sheet and not of the run. That write is append-deduped, so a re-run is safe.

**Fix**

Collect the refusals instead of raising on the first one: report every offending clip id with its lane, keep `--dry-run` read-only and complete, and exit non-zero at the end of the run. That preserves "a refusal costs the run, not the sheet" while making one run enough to fix the bank.

Severity: **Medium**

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
**What is wrong**

`TARGETS` was folded from `{"Documentary": 45, "Neutral": 96}` to `{"Neutral": 141}`, with the comment claiming that this "is the arithmetic a re-run needs to reproduce it, not a new campaign":

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/make_narration_bank.py#L64-L72

The reasoning for folding rather than dropping is sound. The arithmetic is not: the target is not consumed as a lane total, it is consumed as a per-book quota inside the lane.

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/make_narration_bank.py#L112-L117

    want = TARGETS[lane]
    each = max(1, want // len(books))

`len(books)` changed from 1 (Documentary) and 4 (Neutral) to 5, because `voyage-of-the-beagle` moved into the Neutral lane in the same change.

**The concrete failure it causes**

Simulated with the exact expressions from the script:

    before: Documentary: beagle 45 | Neutral: conan 24, slavery 24, franklin 24, walden 24
      total 141
    after : Neutral: beagle 28, conan 28, slavery 28, franklin 28, walden 28
      total 140

Two defects:

1. **140, not 141.** `141 // 5 == 28`, and `28 * 5 == 140`. The floor division loses a clip that the previous split did not lose. The comment's own headline number is never reached.
2. **The per-book composition changes materially.** `voyage-of-the-beagle` goes from 45 lines to 28, and each of the other four books rises from 24 to 28. A re-run therefore renders a different corpus from the one that was audited and closed on 2026-08-04 — which is precisely what the comment says it is preventing.

The rest of the script is internally consistent with the smaller number (`plan[lane] = allocate_engines(n, ...)` uses the actual `n` selected), so nothing crashes. The failure is silent: a re-run claiming to reproduce `delivery-v1-narration-r2` produces a different bank.

**Fix**

Either size per book rather than per lane (a `PER_BOOK` map that records the closed round's actual 45/24/24/24/24), or use a largest-remainder split of `want` across books so the total is exactly `want`. A test asserting `sum(selected per book) == sum(TARGETS.values())` would have caught both halves.

Severity: **Medium**

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
**What is wrong**

PR #39 closes the retirement at `register_audition`, on the premise that it is "the actual unguarded write". `scripts/synthesis/stage_pool.py` is another one, and it was not touched.

1. The CLI still offers the retired lane. `LANES` is the FULL vocabulary, not the assignable set:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/stage_pool.py#L116

    from matcha.delivery import DELIVERY_LANES as LANES

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/stage_pool.py#L294

    ap.add_argument("--mark-delivery", metavar="LANE", choices=LANES, ...)

so `--mark-delivery Documentary` is an accepted argument. This is the same defect the audition app already fixed for its picker (`DELIVERY = (DELIVERY_UNKNOWN, *sorted(ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES))`, `main.py:206`) — the write-shaped surface must offer `ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES`.

2. The staging write takes the lane from persistent ledger state and puts it straight into `ratings.csv`, with no `check_assignable`:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/stage_pool.py#L576-L578

    lane = homogeneous_delivery(rec, led_cache)
    if lane and "delivery" in hdr:
        row["delivery"] = lane

`homogeneous_delivery` reads `delivery_homogeneous` out of the ledger, and the file's own comment (line 92) says a title-level mark "propagates to EVERY clip in the book".

**The concrete failure it causes**

Any ledger entry carrying `delivery_homogeneous: "Documentary"` — written before the 2026-08-10 retirement, when the mark was legal — silently stamps `delivery=Documentary` on every clip staged from that title today. The rows are then ear-certified and refused days later by `merge_expressive_registers.py:315`, with the audition slots already spent: the exact sequence PR #39 argues is worth guarding against at the write site.

I could not confirm whether such an entry exists, because the ledger lives outside the repo (`/data`), so this half is **unverified**. Part 1 is verified from the source: `Documentary in DELIVERY_LANES` is `True`, so argparse accepts it.

The `--mark-delivery` path is additionally gated on the ear having said the same lane on audited rows, and the PR states every Documentary row in `ratings.csv` was relabelled — so re-marking is hard to reach *today*. That makes it a data-shaped guard, not a contract one: it is restored by any restore of a pre-retirement `.bak` sheet, which `synth_common.ratings_transaction` writes routinely.

**Fix**

`choices=ACTIVE_DELIVERY_LANES` on `--mark-delivery`, and route the ledger-sourced lane at line 576 through `check_assignable` so a stale ledger entry fails loudly at staging rather than silently at the merge.

Related to #12, whose enumeration of loose ends named `NARRATION_LANES`, a `book_ingest` lane-pick site, and the audition picker — not this one.

Severity: **Medium**

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
**What is wrong**

The new refusal in `mix_for_lane` is keyed on a locally hand-written normalisation table rather than on the contract's own normalisation:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/ref_select.py#L404-L412

    key = {"dialogue": "Dialogue", "speech": "Speech", "neutral": "Neutral",
           "documentary": "Documentary", "newscaster": "Newscaster"}.get(
               str(lane).lower(), lane)
    if key in _RETIRED_LANES:
        check_assignable(key)

`matcha.delivery.check_assignable` — the function this defers to for the message — normalises differently:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/matcha/delivery.py#L162-L167

    lane = str(lane).strip()

It strips. `mix_for_lane` does not, so the two disagree on any lane with surrounding whitespace, and the disagreement falls open.

**The concrete failure it causes**

Reproduced against this commit:

    mix_for_lane(" Documentary ") is ENGINE_MIX        -> True
    allocate_engines(10, lane=" Documentary")
      -> {qwen: 3, chatterbox: 3, zonos: 2, orpheus: 1, moss_vg: 1}

That is exactly the outcome the docstring says the refusal exists to prevent — "falling back would deal engines into it and buy renders that nothing may then label" — reached by a leading space. Lane strings come from JSON manifests and CSV cells (`stage_pool` calls `.strip()` on `r.get("delivery")` for precisely this reason), so a padded lane is a realistic input, not an invented one.

`"DOCUMENTARY"` is correctly refused, because `.lower()` hits the table. It is only the whitespace axis that leaks.

**A second, latent half**

The five-entry lowercase table is another restatement of the delivery vocabulary in a repo whose stated core defect class is a forked vocabulary. If a lane is ever appended to `DELIVERY_LANES` and later retired, `mix_for_lane(lane.lower())` will not find it in the table, will not match `_RETIRED_LANES`, and will silently fall back — and the new test `test_a_retired_lane_has_no_mix_and_cannot_be_allocated`, which parametrises over `RETIRED_LANES` and checks both `lane` and `lane.lower()`, will then fail pointing at the mapping table rather than at the guard.

**Fix**

Normalise once, up front — `lane = str(lane).strip()` before the table lookup — and ideally derive the lowercase mapping from `DELIVERY_LANES` (`{ln.lower(): ln for ln in DELIVERY_LANES}`) instead of typing it out.

Severity: **Low**

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
**What is wrong**

The helper that both new `register_audition` guard tests depend on obtains the module under test with `importorskip`:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/tests/test_delivery_channel.py#L205

    mod = pytest.importorskip("register_audition")

`pytest.importorskip` converts any `ImportError` raised while importing the module into a **skip**, not a failure. `register_audition` imports `synth_common` and, as of this PR, `matcha.delivery` — and it resolves both through two `sys.path.insert` calls whose targets depend on `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[...]`.

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/02754f6649fd657fb5b5c020435d5276e1373989/scripts/synthesis/register_audition.py#L40-L47

**The concrete failure it causes**

If the new `from matcha.delivery import check_assignable` line is deleted, or the `parents[2]` path insert is broken by a file move, or `synth_common` picks up a dependency that is not installed on the CI image, then:

- `test_the_synthesis_writer_refuses_a_retired_lane` skips,
- `test_the_synthesis_writer_still_pre_fills_an_assignable_lane` skips,

and the suite reports green while the guard those two tests exist to prove is not running at all. That is the same failure shape as issue #27 ("no guard test: reintroducing the bug leaves the whole suite green"), except it arrives silently after the test was written.

The other `importorskip` calls in this file are defensible — `book_ingest`, `ref_select`, `stage_pool` are consumers being checked for consistency, and skipping when they are unavailable is a reasonable degradation. `register_audition` here is the subject, not a dependency, and a subject that cannot be imported is a failing test.

**Fix**

Import `register_audition` with a plain `importlib.import_module` (or a bare `import`) so an import error fails the test, and keep `importorskip` for genuinely optional third-party dependencies. If some environments truly cannot import it, gate on the specific missing dependency by name rather than on "anything went wrong".

Severity: **Low**

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` could not be applied — the label does not exist in this repo and creating it is not permitted from the review sandbox (same as #27/#28/#29). Please create it and apply it here.

**What is wrong**

Splitting "Emilia rows dropped on digits" into a v5 entry and two v6 entries fixes the collision **for the phrasings that exist today**, and re-creates it for one that does not exist yet but is one wording away.

The v5 entry refuses the "N of the M" idiom outright:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/scripts/test_doc_claims.py#L184-L190

```python
"scope": r"Emilia|emilia|13,141|digit rows|D-M3",
"patterns": [r"(?<!of the )(?<![\d,])([\d,]+) (?:rows )?dropped on digits", ...]
```

The v6 entries **claim** that idiom, and their scope carries the bare finding id `D-M3` — which is not a v6 marker. It is the rule id, and every v5 statement of this fact carries it too:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/scripts/test_doc_claims.py#L204-L229

The file argues this is safe:

> It pulls a few v5 lines into scope, and that is harmless BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck — none of them is written in the "N of the M" or parenthetical-breakdown form these patterns require.

That is harmless by the **current wording**, not by construction. Nothing holds the wording.

**The concrete failure it causes**

Reproduced against this commit, feeding one v5 sentence in the "N of the M" idiom to the registry exactly as it now stands:

```
line: "1,676 of the 13,141 rows dropped on digits (D-M3)"

v6 append rows dropped on digits:    in-scope=True   captures ['1,676']   -> compared against 6
v6 append rows staged (candidates):  in-scope=True   captures ['13,141']  -> compared against 832
Emilia rows dropped on digits (v5):  captures []                          -> not checked at all
```

Two false failures on a **correct** v5 statement, and the entry that owns that fact cannot see it. That is the "two correct documents, a permanently red gate" failure this change exists to end, moved one phrasing to the left.

It is not a hypothetical wording. `notes/training-sources.md:129` already writes the neighbouring fact in precisely that idiom, on the same line as the digit count:

> 2,144 of the 13,141 keeps did not make it: **1,676 carry digits** (D-M3 — the tokenizer …)

so a routine edit regularising the two halves of that sentence turns the gate red, and the only way back is to edit a document that was right.

The second half is a silent miss, which is the worse direction: with `(?<!of the )` in place, a **wrong** v5 digit count written as "1,677 of the 13,141 dropped on digits" is invisible to the v5 entry by construction.

**Fix**

Scope the v6 entries on markers that are actually v6 (`expressive`, `append set`, `v6`) and drop the bare `D-M3`; where a line genuinely names no corpus (`notes/STATE.md:313`), give that line a corpus marker rather than giving the registry a rule id. If `D-M3` must stay in v6's scope, the v5 entry has to accept the "N of the M" idiom with an `Emilia`/`13,141`-anchored pattern, so the two entries cannot both be wrong about the same sentence.

**Severity: Medium.** No failure on today's text; it is a latent red-gate / silent-miss pair inside the file whose thesis is that a gate nobody can turn green stops being a gate. Found reviewing PR #40.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` could not be applied — the label does not exist in this repo (same as #27/#28/#29).

**What is wrong**

`scripts/test_doc_claims.py` is reached from the suite only through `tests/test_gate_scripts.py::test_data_gated_gate`, which runs it as a subprocess and **skips whenever the corpus artifacts are absent** — i.e. on every machine except ai-lab-0.

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/tests/test_gate_scripts.py#L77-L86

Verified on this commit:

```
tests/test_gate_scripts.py::test_data_gated_gate[test_doc_claims.py-prereqs0] SKIPPED
```

That skip is right for the *data* half — "the corpus is not on this machine" is not a finding, as the comment says. But the registry is now two things in one file: a set of artifact reads, and **a body of subtle regex** — three lookbehinds, five scope alternations, nine patterns, and an explicit rule ("never scope a fact on the value it checks") that is enforced by nothing. The regex half needs no artifacts at all and is currently guarded nowhere.

The cost is already documented in this very change. The first draft scoped the v6 entries on the literal `832`, so corrupting `832` removed the line from its own scope and **the gate went green** — a hole found only by testing the RED direction. That probe was run by hand and **nothing was committed that re-runs it**. Re-introduce `832` into a scope tomorrow and `pytest tests/ -q` is green on every machine, and skipped rather than run on the one machine that could tell.

**The concrete failure it causes**

Three mutations that a reviewer or CI cannot currently detect, each restoring a bug this change was written to fix:

1. put `832` back in the v6 scope — a wrong `832` deletes its own check (the hole the author found by hand);
2. delete `(?<![\d,])` from the v5 patterns — the capture shifts one digit right and reports `3,141` for `of the 13,141`, which I confirmed against this commit:
   `re.findall(r"(?<!of the )([\d,]+) (?:rows )?dropped on digits", "1,676 of the 13,141 rows dropped on digits")` returns `['3,141']`;
3. put the bare `digit` back in the v5 scope — the original two-generation collision returns.

All three leave `519 passed`.

**Fix**

Split the pure-regex half out into a normal `tests/` test with no artifact dependency: a table of synthetic doc lines with the value each fact should capture, plus the negative cases (a v5 line must not be captured by a v6 entry; corrupting a value must not remove its line from scope). Both directions, and the red one is the one that matters — the author's own note says "proving a gate passes proves nothing; prove it fails". Roughly 40 lines, runs everywhere, and it is what makes the manual verification in this PR durable.

**Severity: Medium.** No wrong behaviour today; the defect is that the fix has no guard and the discovered hole can be reopened silently — the same shape as #27. Found reviewing PR #40.

issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` could not be applied — the label does not exist in this repo (same as #27/#28/#29).

**What is wrong**

`notes/README.md:29` contradicts itself inside one sentence:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/notes/README.md#L27-L31

> v6 (+expressive-registers, **832 rows appended** — 1,004 eligible, less 158 duplicate-audio, less 14 over `MAX_SECONDS`) is **BUILT** as `libritts_r_emilia_expressive_vat_v6` (41,937 train / 1,331 val, n_spks 3,326)

41,937 + 1,331 = 43,268, and v5 is 42,442 (`notes/training-sources.md:44`), so **826** rows were appended. The same sentence carries both the wrong claim and the arithmetic that refutes it. The root README states it correctly:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/README.md#L75

> **826 appended rows**, 816 of them delivery-labelled across four lanes, out of 1,004 eligible keeps (158 already in v5, 14 over-length, 6 dropped on digits)

832 is the **staged** count (1,004 − 158 − 14); 826 is what survived the digit drop. Two READMEs disagree about the size of v6's append set — the exact fork class the doc-claims gate exists to catch.

**The concrete failure it causes**

It is invisible to the gate, including after this change. The registry now reads `expressive.candidates` (832) but **not** `expressive.kept` (826):

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/scripts/test_doc_claims.py#L222-L229

and none of its four patterns matches the phrasing "832 rows appended" — `rows to append` and `append set is settled at **N rows**` are the staged idioms. So the gate's v6 coverage checks the number the documents agree on and skips the one they disagree about. Both are real keys emitted by the same builder (`scripts/merge_expressive_registers.py:455-456`, `"candidates": len(rows)` / `"kept": len(new)`), so the fact costs one registry entry.

Anyone sizing rung 2 from `notes/README.md` over-counts the append set by 6 and, more importantly, inherits the belief that the digit drop did not happen — 832 is the count *before* the D-M3 filter that this same PR spent an entire registry entry making checkable.

The PR that found this named it in its own "noticed, deliberately not changed" list. Filing so it is not lost.

**Fix**

Change `notes/README.md:29` to "832 rows staged, 826 appended", and add an `expressive.kept` fact with patterns for the `N appended rows` / `N rows appended` idioms.

**Severity: Medium.** Documentation-only, but it is a live fork between two READMEs about a built corpus, and the gate's new coverage steps around it. Found reviewing PR #40.
