issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` could not be applied — the label does not exist in this repo (same as #27/#28/#29).

**What is wrong**

Two of the registry's facts read a key that the builder only writes when the count is non-zero.

`scripts/merge_expressive_registers.py` accumulates drops in a `collections.Counter` and serialises it with `dict(dropped)`:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/scripts/merge_expressive_registers.py#L455-L458

```python
"candidates": len(rows),
"kept": len(new),
"dropped": dict(dropped),
```

A `Counter` has no entry for a reason that never fired, so `expressive.dropped.digits` is present in the current report only because 6 rows happened to carry digits. `scripts/merge_emilia_corpus.py:410` does the same for `emilia.dropped.digits`.

The reader walks the key path and lets `KeyError` escape to the caller:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/scripts/test_doc_claims.py#L69-L85

which `main()` turns into a failure, deliberately:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/scripts/test_doc_claims.py#L299-L304

```
{fact['name']}: cannot read the artifact ({e}). A fact whose source is missing is not a passing fact.
```

**The concrete failure it causes**

Rebuild v6 (or v7) from inputs that carry no digits — which is the *desired* state, since D-M3 exists to make digit-carrying rows go away — and the gate reports:

```
FAIL — 1 claim(s) disagree with the artifact:
  v6 append rows dropped on digits: cannot read the artifact ('digits'). A fact whose source is missing is not a passing fact.
```

A correct corpus, correct documents, and a red gate whose message says the artifact is missing when the artifact is there and simply says zero. That is the same "a gate nobody can turn green" failure this change was written to end, and the only way to clear it is to edit the registry — which the file's own footer tells the reader to do only "if the artifact was rebuilt", so the wrong lesson is available too.

I could not reproduce this end-to-end: `data/` is untracked and absent in the review container, so the artifact side of every fact is unverified here. The mechanism is read off the builder and the reader, both in-tree.

**Fix**

Either read the drop counters with a zero default (`node.get(part, 0)` for the final hop of a `dropped.*` key), or have both builders seed every known drop reason at zero so the schema is fixed rather than data-dependent. The second is better — it also makes "no rows were dropped for reason X" a statement the report actually makes.

**Severity: Low.** Latent; fires on the next rebuild that drops nothing on digits. Found reviewing PR #40.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` could not be applied — the label does not exist in this repo (same as #27/#28/#29).

**What is wrong**

`DATA_GATED` now carries a list of prerequisites, and the runner skips the whole gate if **any** of them is missing:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/tests/test_gate_scripts.py#L77-L86

```python
for env_var, default in prereqs:
    target = os.environ.get(env_var, default)
    if not os.path.exists(target):
        pytest.skip(...)
```

That is the right call given the script's all-or-nothing behaviour (a fact whose source is missing is a failure), and the CHANGELOG argues for it. What is not stated anywhere is the price: prerequisite coverage is now the **intersection**, not the union.

**The concrete failure it causes**

On a machine holding v5 but not v6 — a partial `data/` mount, a mid-build host, a rollback to the previous corpus, or ai-lab-0 itself between `merge_emilia_corpus` and `merge_expressive_registers` — the gate went from *checking all ten v5 facts* to *checking nothing*, and it reports that as a skip. The skip line names only the first missing prerequisite, so the reader sees "SONORA_CORPUS_V6 target not present" and has no signal that the v5 half was checkable and was dropped.

This grows with every corpus generation: at v7 the gate runs only where v5, v6 and v7 all live, which is one machine on a good day. The gate that exists because "only a check is continuous" becomes conditional on the union of every artifact it has ever read.

**Fix**

Push the prerequisite down to the fact. Give each `FACTS` entry the artifact path it needs and let the script skip-with-notice the facts whose artifact is absent (printed, never silent, and non-zero exit only if a *present* artifact disagrees) — then `test_data_gated_gate` needs no prerequisite list at all and a v5-only machine still enforces v5. Failing that, split `DATA_GATED` per corpus and pass the registry a filter, so a missing v6 skips v6's two facts rather than all twelve.

**Severity: Low.** No wrong result; a coverage reduction that is invisible at the point it happens. Found reviewing PR #40.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
> **Ledger note:** intended label `review-finding` could not be applied — the label does not exist in this repo (same as #27/#28/#29).

**What is wrong**

The corrected `Documentary` note in the v6 data config mixes three populations in four lines without naming any of them:

https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/ac3965af7a79d7d831a77d76312ca94294018da5/configs/data/libritts_r_emilia_expressive_vat_v6.yaml#L52-L59

```yaml
# DELIVERY: Dialogue 344 · Neutral 328 · Newscaster 76 · Speech 68 · blank 10.
# `Documentary` was RETIRED into Neutral (owner, 2026-08-10) — **154 rows in `ratings.csv`,
# all 154 reassigned to Neutral**, of which 82 were in this append set.
# ... Newscaster is 76 on BOTH sides of the retirement while Neutral goes 251 → 328
# (333 less the five it lost to digits).
```

The three populations, worked out from the numbers themselves:

* **154** — `ratings.csv`, the whole rated bank.
* **82** — the *staged* append set. `notes/quality-gap-plan.md:289` gives the pre-retirement lane table as `Neutral 251 · Documentary 82 · Newscaster 76 · Speech 69`, and with Dialogue 344 and blank 10 that sums to **832**, the staged count.
* **328 / 76 / 68** — the lane table at the top of the same comment sums to **826**, the built corpus, after the six D-M3 drops.

So "of which 82 were in this append set" is a count over 832 asserted inside a header describing the 826 rows the config actually loads. The comment's own parenthesis proves the two differ: Neutral is `333 less the five it lost to digits`, and Speech goes 69 → 68 for the sixth.

**The concrete failure it causes**

The five digit-dropped Neutral rows are drawn from a bucket that is 251 pre-existing Neutral plus 82 ex-Documentary; nothing records which side they came from. The number of Documentary-origin rows that actually reached `train_op.txt` is therefore somewhere in **77–82** and is stated nowhere, while the config asserts 82 as a property of "this append set".

This is a small instance of the population confusion already open as #32 (statistics over `labels_v6.jsonl`'s 846 rows reported as facts about the 832-row append set) — same axis, one generation further down: 846 → 832 staged → 826 built, and each of the three gets quoted as "the append set" somewhere in the tree. Anyone reconciling the retirement against the shipped corpus differences the wrong pair and finds a discrepancy of up to five rows with nothing to attribute it to.

**Fix**

Name the population at each number: "154 rows in `ratings.csv`, 82 of them in the 832-row staged append set, of which 77–82 survive the D-M3 drop into the 826 rows this config loads" — or state which side the five drops came from, which the build log knows.

**Severity: Low.** Documentation-only, and the arithmetic in the comment is internally consistent; the defect is that three populations share one name. Found reviewing PR #40.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
NOTE: intended label `review-finding` does not exist in this repo and could not be created; please apply it.

The 2026-08-11 wiring change added a loud stop when the *campaign* EIV file is missing a combination head ([qc_verdict.py L216-L230](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/qc_verdict.py#L216-L230)). The *anchor* side of the same computation was left exactly as it was:

```python
for h in heads:
    anchor[h] = gs([d.get(h, 0.0) for d in joined])
```

[build_anchors, qc_verdict.py L153-L154](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/qc_verdict.py#L153-L154)

**Why this is worse than the bug it was written beside**

`gs()` returns `(mean, std + 1e-9)`. When a combination head is absent from the anchor corpus, every value is `0.0`, so `gs` returns `(0.0, 1e-9)` and `z(h, x)` becomes `x * 1e9`. That factor lands in the V dot product:

```python
"V": float(np.dot(W, [z(h, e.get(h, 0.0)) for h in HEADS]))
```

so |V| is astronomically larger than `--z-confirm` (default 0.25) for every clip. The magnitude test always passes and the sign is whatever the weights produce. **The V axis stops being a measurement and becomes a constant verdict.**

The revisit-v1 defect this change documents made V *fail* silently. This one makes V ***pass*** silently, which is strictly harder to notice: a healthy-looking keep rate is exactly what nobody investigates.

**Reproduced**

Stubbed anchor files, `LIB_EIV` carrying 3 of the 6 heads the combo needs, campaign EIV file complete (so the new guard sees nothing absent):

```
id                         axis verdicts                            keep
clip0                      V:ok(-0.9->-100000000.20) A:FAIL(+0.8->-0.41) T:FAIL(+0.7->-0.75) False
...
direction failures among hard-pass clips: 4 clip(s) - V:0 A:4 T:4
QC-VERDICT-DONE          (exit 0)

measured_z row0: {"T": -0.745, "A": -0.409, "V": -100000000.20480798}
axis_checks row0: {"V": true, "A": false, "T": false}
```

A `measured_z` of -1.0e8 is written into `qc_verdicts.jsonl` and reported as `V:ok`, and `by_axis` shows `V:0` failures.

**This is not hypothetical**

`scripts/eiv_score.sh` records in its own header that the corpus anchor is exactly in this shape:

> which is why the corpus scores ended up split across two files with different head sets (corpus_v1.jsonl and corpus_families.jsonl) and no record of the invocation

`build_anchors` merges those two with a dict splat of `lib_eiv[wav]` over `lib_fam.get(wav, {})`. A head absent from both gives the full 1e9 blowup; a head present in `corpus_families.jsonl` for only *some* wavs gives a quieter version - the 0.0 fill contaminates that heads anchor mean and std, so every campaign V is offset and rescaled against a corrupted zero.

**Suggested direction**

Apply the same refusal to the anchor that L216 now applies to the campaign file: after the merge, assert every combo head is present on every joined row, and stop naming the corpus file rather than filling with 0.0. A `std` that collapses to the 1e-9 epsilon is on its own a signal that a channel carries no information and must not be divided by.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
NOTE: intended label `review-finding` does not exist in this repo and could not be created; please apply it.

Two defects with one root: **unmeasured** and **pointed the wrong way** produce identical output.

**1. The head guard is vacuous when the file is empty**

```python
absent = sorted({h for d in eiv_rows for h in need if h not in d})
if absent:
    sys.exit("QC-VERDICT-FAIL: ...")
```

[qc_verdict.py L216-L230](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/qc_verdict.py#L216-L230)

The comprehension iterates over rows. With zero rows the set is empty, `absent` is falsy, and the guard - the centrepiece of this change - does not fire. The stage then runs to completion against no scores at all.

**2. A missing EIV row scores as a failed axis**

`raw_measures` returns `{}` when `eiv_for(r)` is None. In `axis_verdicts` that gives `got is None` for a directed axis (check False) and `False` for a near-neutral axis. So every axis of every unscored clip fails.

**Reproduced - empty eiv_scores.jsonl, 4 directed clips, exit 0**

```
clip0                      V:FAIL(-0.9->--) A:FAIL(+0.8->--) T:FAIL(+0.7->--) False
clip1                      V:FAIL(-0.9->--) A:FAIL(+0.8->--) T:FAIL(+0.7->--) False
clip2                      V:FAIL(-0.9->--) A:FAIL(+0.8->--) T:FAIL(+0.7->--) False
clip3                      V:FAIL(-0.9->--) A:FAIL(+0.8->--) T:FAIL(+0.7->--) False
0/4 keeps -> keeps.jsonl
direction failures among hard-pass clips: 4 clip(s) - V:4 A:4 T:4
appended 4 new ids to .../qc_flags.txt (0 already present)
QC-VERDICT-DONE

EXIT: 0
qc_flags.txt: [clip0, clip1, clip2, clip3]
```

**Reproduced - partial coverage (2 of 4 clips scored), exit 0**

```
clip0                      V:FAIL(-0.9->+0.00) A:FAIL(+0.8->-1.39) T:FAIL(+0.7->+0.24) False
clip1                      V:FAIL(-0.9->+0.00) A:FAIL(+0.8->-1.39) T:FAIL(+0.7->+0.24) False
clip2                      V:FAIL(-0.9->--) A:FAIL(+0.8->--) T:FAIL(+0.7->--) False
clip3                      V:FAIL(-0.9->--) A:FAIL(+0.8->--) T:FAIL(+0.7->--) False
direction failures among hard-pass clips: 4 clip(s) - V:4 A:4 T:4
```

`clip2` and `clip3` were never measured. They land in the same `direction failures` count, the same `by_axis` tallies, and the same `qc_flags.txt` as `clip0` and `clip1`, which were measured and genuinely disagreed.

**Concrete failure**

`eiv_score.sh` exits non-zero only when the `docker run` fails. A container that comes up, loads the model and scores nothing - empty `qc_filelist.txt`, unreadable wavs, an OOM-skip, a truncated resume - exits 0. `synth_bank.sh` then takes the success branch and `qc_verdict` reports a **100% direction-failure rate**, floods `qc_flags.txt`, and writes an empty `keeps.jsonl`, all with `QC-VERDICT-DONE` and exit 0.

That is exactly the misreading this change was written to end. Its own docstring, on the revisit-v1 incident:

> Its V axis was failing for want of a head, and reading as engines ignoring direction.

The same sentence now applies to a clip that was never scored.

**Suggested direction**

- Refuse (or announce loudly) when `eiv_rows` is empty, and when the row count is materially below the `qc_filelist.txt` line count.
- Distinguish `unscored` from `failed` in `axis_checks` (e.g. `None`), keep unscored clips out of the `direction failures` tally and out of `qc_flags.txt`, and print an explicit `N clip(s) had no EIV row` line beside the existing `undirected` line.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
NOTE: intended label `review-finding` does not exist in this repo and could not be created; please apply it.

The new staleness guard compares each wav mtime against the mtime of the whole scores file:

```python
eiv_mtime = os.path.getmtime(args.eiv)
stale = [r["id"] for r in rows
         if eiv_for(r) is not None and os.path.isfile(r["wav_abs"])
         and os.path.getmtime(r["wav_abs"]) > eiv_mtime]
```

[qc_verdict.py L250-L262](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/qc_verdict.py#L250-L262)

**The problem**

`args.eiv` is a single append-only file whose mtime is the time of the **most recent append**, not the time any particular clip was scored. In `synth_bank.sh` the wiring is:

```
elif ! "$SONORA/scripts/eiv_score.sh" "$EIV_SCORES" ... ; then
  ...
elif ! "$PY" .../qc_verdict.py --campaign-dir "$CAMPAIGN_DIR" --eiv "$EIV_SCORES" --append-flags; then
```

[synth_bank.sh L341-L347](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/synth_bank.sh#L341-L347)

`eiv_score.sh` runs immediately before `qc_verdict.py` and appends to `$EIV_SCORES`. Any bank with at least one newly-scored clip - the normal case - leaves the file mtime at *now*, above every wav mtime. `stale` is empty by construction.

**The scenario it was written for is the one it misses**

The guard exists because a rerolled clip keeps its path and `eiv_score.py` resumes by path, so the reroll is skipped and judged against the previous take. But the reroll happens *before* the render pass finishes, so by the time `eiv_score.sh` runs and appends the other new clips, the file is newer than the rerolled wav. The rerolled clip is silently judged on stale scores, which is the precise outcome the guard was added to announce.

**Reproduced**

```
D - reroll staleness under the order synth_bank.sh uses
before eiv_score.sh re-runs -> guard fired: True
after  eiv_score.sh re-runs -> guard fired: False
```

Same campaign, same rerolled clip0 with a wav newer than its own score row. The only change between the two lines is one appended row for an unrelated clip, i.e. exactly what `eiv_score.sh` does on every pipeline run.

**Suggested direction**

File mtime is the wrong clock. Either stamp each EIV row with the scored wav mtime (or a content hash) at scoring time and compare per row, or have `eiv_score.py` resume on `(path, mtime)` rather than path alone so a rerolled clip is re-scored instead of skipped. As written the guard reports on a condition the pipeline cannot reach and reads as coverage that is not there.

`test_the_direction_check_is_advisory_and_the_quality_gate_is_not` is described as protecting the property that the whole change turns on - stage 2 must never stop the bank. Its search window is derived from the *last* line of the block it means to cover:

```python
verdict = _first_line_with(BANK, "qc_verdict.py", extra="--eiv")
register = _first_line_with(BANK, "register_audition.py")
stage2 = [c for n, c in cmds if verdict is not None and verdict <= n < register]
offenders = [c for c in stage2 if c.split("#")[0].strip().startswith("exit")
             or " exit " in c]
```

[test_audit_sampling.py L406-L430](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/tests/test_audit_sampling.py#L406-L430)

**Measured window**

Resolved against the committed `synth_bank.sh`:

```
gate 264   eiv 341   verdict 346   register 386
stage2 window lines: 346 -> 386, 10 commands
```

The stage-2 block starts at line 280. The window starts at 346. Lines **280-345** - the `--count-directed` probe, the whole `case` statement, the probe-failed branch, the zero/real-audio branch, the `--print-heads` branch and both `eiv_score.sh` failure branches - are **outside** the guard. Of the roughly 75 new shell lines, the guard sees the last ten, three of which are `echo`, plus `fi`, `;;` and `esac`, plus two commands belonging to the *next* stage (`qc_engine_defects.py` and the `register audition` banner).

**Proven by mutation**

Inserting `exit 1` into the `eiv_score` failure branch (line 343) - the single most plausible future edit, someone deciding a failed scoring pass should stop the pipeline:

```
27 passed in 0.13s
```

All green. The direction check now aborts the bank, and the test whose docstring calls this difference *the whole fix* does not notice.

Positive control - the same `exit 1` inserted six lines later, at 348, inside the window:

```
AssertionError: the direction check can stop the bank: exit 1 - it is advisory,
and a mislabelled clip must not be pulled out of the queue
1 failed, 26 passed
```

So the assertion works; it is simply pointed at the wrong range.

**Suggested direction**

Anchor the window to the *start* of stage 2 rather than its last command - the `--count-directed` invocation, or the `== qc verdicts` banner - and bound it at the first stage-3 command rather than at `register_audition.py`, so `qc_engine_defects` is not being checked by a test that names stage 2.

issues.author: app/claude
issues.body:
NOTE: intended label `review-finding` does not exist in this repo and could not be created; please apply it.

`intended_labels` accepts a value only if it is already an `int` or `float`:

```python
lab = row.get("intended") or {}
out = {}
for ax in AXES:
    v = lab.get(ax)
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool):
        out[ax] = float(v)
return out
```

[qc_verdict.py L104-L110](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/qc_verdict.py#L104-L110)

`--count-directed` is `sum(1 for r in rows if intended_labels(r))`, so a bank whose `intended` values are JSON strings counts as **0 directed clips** - indistinguishable from a bank with no `intended` key at all.

`synth_bank.sh` then takes the zero branch:

```
0)
  echo "  no intended V/A/T in $CAMPAIGN_DIR/qc_measures.jsonl (real-audio bank)"
  echo "  - nothing to confirm; direction check skipped."
```

[synth_bank.sh L320-L325](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/synth_bank.sh#L320-L325)

**Reproduced**

Four clips, each carrying `intended` as strings:

```
E - intended present but non-numeric (strings)
--count-directed prints: 0 -> shell takes the 0 branch
```

The log then asserts `(real-audio bank)` about a fully directed synthetic campaign, the whole stage is skipped, and the round is spent for `gate_calibration` with nothing frozen.

**Why this matters despite being narrow**

The adjacent branch is written specifically to refuse this collapse:

> "The probe did not answer" is NOT "this bank has no labels", and collapsing the two would rebuild the hole this fix closes: a directed bank would sail past a message saying it was real audio.

The zero branch has the same hole through a different door: **the probe answered, and the answer was wrong.** A silent zero asserts a positive fact about the bank that nothing verified. The same applies to the `os.path.isfile(measures_path)` fallback at [L200](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/blob/dde082c76d334d1b174fe24f9a7f23700decd38f/scripts/synthesis/qc_verdict.py#L200) - a missing measures file also yields `0` and therefore also prints `(real-audio bank)`. Stage 1 currently makes that unreachable, but it is the same shape and it is one refactor away.

Severity is low today because the writers (`make_bulk_bank.py`, `make_narration_bank.py`, `make_quote_pilot_bank.py`, ...) all emit rounded floats. Nothing enforces that, and `intended_labels` is the only place that would notice.

**Suggested direction**

Separate `no intended key` from `intended key present but unusable`. Count a row as directed when `intended` exists at all, and have the second case raise or announce by name rather than being absorbed into the same `0` the real-audio banks produce.

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
Deferred from **#78** (merged as `330fad4`); the review thread is [here](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/78#discussion_r3775901258) and was left unresolved deliberately. Verified against `main` at the merge commit before filing.

## The defect

`_argv_printed_filter` in `tests/test_stage_coverage.py` has two halves that run on **opposite premises about the same input**.

`shell=True` with a one-element list is a command *line*: POSIX hands element 0 to `/bin/sh -c` and the remaining elements become `$0`/`$1`. #78 corrected the **exemption test** for that (it uses `is_wholly_printed`, which treats element 0 as a shell line). It did **not** correct the **haystack choice** two lines below, which still returns `survivors = None` on the grounds that

> a **list** argv is already split, so only element 0 is the verb

— the premise the line above it retracts. The `None` sends the caller to the whole unparsed call rather than to what survived the printed-text filter.

## Reproduction (verified on `main` @ `330fad4`)

Byte-identical shell lines, opposite verdicts:

```python
os.system("echo at $(date) rerun python scripts/stages/qc_gate.py")
# -> []                                                    correct: only prints

subprocess.run(["echo at $(date) rerun python scripts/stages/qc_gate.py"], shell=True)
# -> ['x.py:2: run(...) launches qc_gate.py']               FALSE POSITIVE
```

Direction is a **false red** on a line that only prints, so it is a nuisance rather than a hole — which is why it was LOW/MEDIUM and not a blocker. Note it is **not a regression**: the behaviour is unchanged from `d2c6113`; what #78 changed is that the docstring justifying it is now self-contradicting.

## The fix worth making

Not another special case. A one-element `shell=True` list **is** a shell line and should go down the string path entirely, rather than the list path learning to imitate it one predicate at a time. Concretely: detect `shell=True` in the call's keywords, and when element 0 is a lone string constant, treat it exactly as a string argv (localised `survivors`, unioned with `args[1:]` and keyword values as the string path already does).

Whichever way it goes, the docstring at `_argv_printed_filter` must stop asserting "a list argv is already split" without qualification — that sentence is what made the inconsistency invisible.

## Context worth reading first

This sits inside the larger design question recorded on #68: `_invocations` and `stage_launch_offenders` have **opposite risk profiles** (a false positive silently unwires a stage in one, and is a visible red in the other) yet share one increasingly clever printed-text function. Fixing this issue in isolation is fine and cheap; doing it as part of that split is better.

⚠ Any change here needs a fixture in **both** directions and a mutation that is red without it — #78's four rounds are the argument, and #68 carries the rules that came out of them.
issues.title: Stage-wiring guard: the string and shell=True-list paths disagree on identical shell lines

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
Deferred from **#78** (merged as `330fad4`). Two review threads, one root cause:
[backtick separator](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/78#discussion_r3775903339) · [`_RECIPE_ECHO` boundary](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/78#discussion_r3775905579). Both left unresolved deliberately; both re-verified against the merge commit before filing.

**The code is correct at every site today.** What is missing is any test that would notice if it stopped being. Each of these can be reverted on its own and the suite stays at its normal `1073 passed / 5 failed` (the 5 being the pre-existing `data/libritts_r_vat_v4/*` missing-corpus failures).

## 1. The substitution separator, backtick half — `tests/test_audit_sampling.py`

`_without_printed_text` appends the recursed body of a command substitution with a trailing space, at **two** call sites — `$( … )` and `` ` … ` ``. Without it, two adjacent substitutions concatenate their survivors and fabricate a name present in neither body (`qc_` + `gate.py` → `qc_gate.py`, a false launch).

Verified: reverting **only** the backtick site → `1073 passed`. No fixture anywhere puts two backtick substitutions next to each other; the row added in #78 is the `$( )$( )` spelling only.

Needs: a `` `x scripts/stages/qc_` ``/`` `gate.py y` `` adjacent-backtick row alongside the existing `$( )$( )` one.

## 2. `_RECIPE_ECHO`'s verb boundary — `tests/test_audit_sampling.py`

`_RECIPE_ECHO` uses `(?![\w/.-])` rather than `\b` after the verb. ⚠ Note this is **not** the same defect as `_ECHO_HEAD`'s: `_RECIPE_ECHO` has no path prefix, so the interior-`/` case cannot arise there. What the class actually buys is the `.`/`-` half, and it is load-bearing:

```
Makefile line:  \t@echo.py python scripts/stages/qc_gate.py

  (?![\w/.-])   -> ['Makefile:1: @echo.py python scripts/stages/qc_gate.py']
  \b            -> []                                    <- the launch is ERASED
```

That is the silent-miss direction — a real launch vanishing because a Makefile recipe happens to invoke a script called `echo.py`. Verified: reverting it to `\b` → `1073 passed`, launch erased.

Needs: a `@echo.py`-style recipe row.

## Root cause — both are gaps in the mutation battery, and both are mechanical

Recorded on #68 as the third and fourth mechanisms behind "a mutation battery is necessary and not sufficient":

* **A fix applied at N sites needs a mutation that reaches all N.** The battery's mutation for the separator is a `str.replace(old, new, 1)` on the append expression — it patches the **first** of two identical call sites, so the backtick half was never mutated.
* **A shared constant is what lets one mutation cover N sites.** `(?![\w/.-])` is hardcoded inline in `_RECIPE_ECHO` instead of interpolating the `_VERB_END` constant used by `_ECHO_HEAD`, so the mutation that flips `_VERB_END` cannot reach it. Interpolating the constant fixes the coverage gap and the duplication at once.

Doing the second one first makes the second fixture almost redundant, which is the better ordering.

## Scope note

The battery itself is **not in the repo** — it lives in a session scratchpad. Making it a committed, runnable target is arguably the real fix and is worth deciding under #68; this issue is only about the two missing fixtures and the shared constant, both of which are small and stand on their own.
issues.title: Two stage-guard fixes are unpinned: reverting either leaves the suite green

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
Deferred from **#78** (merged as `330fad4`); [thread](https://github.com/Artificial-Humanity/Sonora/pull/78#discussion_r3775907476), left unresolved deliberately. Verified against the merge commit.

## The row

`tests/test_stage_coverage.py`, in `test_a_real_launch_in_a_makefile_or_workflow_is_reported`:

```python
("Makefile", "\tpython scripts/echo/qc_gate.py"),           # pre-existing
("Makefile", "\tpython scripts/echo/qc_gate.py --apply"),   # added by #78
```

` --apply` is inert for **both** conjuncts of the branch's append condition (`stage in bare`, and the `(python|\$PY)\S*\s` launcher token) and for all four assertions in the test body including the neutered negative control. Verified — the two rows are the same measurement:

```
'\tpython scripts/echo/qc_gate.py'          -> ['Makefile:1: python scripts/echo/qc_gate.py']
'\tpython scripts/echo/qc_gate.py --apply'  -> ['Makefile:1: python scripts/echo/qc_gate.py --apply']
```

## Why it is worth an issue rather than a shrug

The comment above it claims it is the row that *isolates the erasure defect from the branch's separate launcher-token rule*. That reasoning is sound and it is the reason the row was added — but it applies equally to the row already there, so what actually got added is a duplicate wearing the justification. A later cleanup reading that comment will keep the duplicate and delete the original, or keep both on the strength of it and never notice.

The `$PY` row on the following line **is** carrying new coverage (a different launcher token — and it is what exposed the negative control silently not running on `$PY` lines). That one stays.

## Fix

Delete the ` --apply` row; move the explanatory comment onto the pre-existing row it actually describes.

## The general rule this is an instance of

From #68: **a fixture earns its line only if some mutation is red with it and green without.** That is checkable mechanically over the fixture list, not just over fixes — and this row fails it. Worth running that check across both guard files while here, rather than only on this one row.

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
From the step-4 review of the workflow change (findings 1, 2, 6 and 5). Verified against `main` at the time of filing.

## The problem

The six-step loop is written out in **both** `AGENTS.md` §1 and `notes/reviews/README.md`. That duplication was introduced deliberately — the numbered list is what gets copied, so both copies were made to say the same thing — and it immediately reproduced the failure `AGENTS.md` §3 already warns about, in a hard-won ⚠:

> *"Deliberately not restated here — the same claim in two files drifted three times in one pull request, and after the third correction the two copies contradicted each other."*

**It drifted inside the commit that created it**, twice, both times with the README as the lossy copy:

* **No abort in the README's copy.** `notes/reviews/README.md`'s "The lifecycle" has zero matches for *abort* / *should not land* / *do not push* / *owner* — every path still ends at step 6. That is exactly the state the abort was added to fix, surviving in the file §1 points the reader at.
* **No range fallback in the README's copy.** Its step 2 omits the `origin/main..HEAD` fallback entirely (see the separate issue on `@{push}` for why that matters more than it looks).

## Recommended fix

**`notes/reviews/README.md` stops listing the steps** and points at §1 for the procedure, keeping only what is genuinely local to that directory: the `review-<sha7>` naming rule, the gitignore reasoning, the two-files-per-cycle note, the rebase caveat, and "handoff not a record". Nothing is lost and the loop has one home.

The alternative — a test asserting the two lists agree — guards a duplication that does not need to exist. §3 faced this exact choice and chose de-duplication.

## Also in scope, same class

**The README's SHA diagnostic now self-cancels.** The two ⚠ blocks read *"check whether its SHA is already on `main`"* followed by *"that check gives the wrong answer after a rebase"*, leaving no third thing to do — and the diagnostic is consulted precisely when something went wrong, which is the case it cannot handle. One question that is correct in every case:

> Is its SHA anywhere in `git log origin/main..HEAD`, or on `main`? If neither, the cycle was rebased away or abandoned: delete the file and start again on the current range.

**A grammar defect introduced by the same pass**, `tests/test_stage_coverage.py:783`:

> ``Makefile``, ``.github/workflows/ci.yml`` contains exactly these shapes.

Two subjects, singular verb, comma where "and" belongs — it was a three-item list ending "all contain" before a workflow was deleted from it. Should read *"`Makefile` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` contain exactly these shapes."*

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Fixed. `notes/reviews/README.md` no longer restates the six steps — the procedure lives in AGENTS.md §1 and only there. What stays is what is local to that directory: the `<sha7>` naming rule, the two-files-per-cycle note, the gitignore reasoning, handoff-not-a-record, and the stray-file diagnostic (rephrased so it is also correct after a rebase). Verified by the re-review: nothing load-bearing was lost, and the one clause that had gone — *whether it ended in issues or ended clean* — was restored to §1 step 6, since a clean review is exactly when a worker assumes there is nothing to close.

⚠ **Closed as fixed, not as "cannot recur".** The remedy here is **local git config** (and, for #88's sibling mechanics, a local repo extension) — **none of it travels with the repo**. A fresh clone gets `push.default=simple`, `pull.rebase` unset, and no `extensions.worktreeConfig`, so every one of these traps returns intact. What survives a clone is §1's *documentation* of them, which is why that text stays even though the config makes it moot in this checkout.

issues.title: The commit→review→push loop is stated in two files and has already drifted

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
From the step-4 review of the workflow change (finding 3). **Measured on the branch the rule was written on.**

## The defect

`AGENTS.md` §1 step 2 tells the worker to review `@{push}..HEAD`, offering `origin/main..HEAD` as the fallback *"with no upstream"*. That condition is not the one that fails:

```
$ git rev-parse '@{push}'
fatal: cannot resolve 'simple' push to a single destination

$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref '@{upstream}'
origin/main
```

**The branch has an upstream and `@{push}` still fails.** So a worker asks "do I have an upstream?", correctly answers *yes*, uses `@{push}..HEAD`, and gets a fatal error with no documented recovery. `notes/reviews/README.md`'s copy of step 2 omits the fallback altogether, so it simply fails.

This is the shape §5 names: the classification is right — review the range you are about to push, which is the fix for a real defect — and the instruction sitting beside it errors out on the branch it was written on.

## Fix

Make **`origin/main..HEAD` the primary form.** It always resolves under this model, because step 6 pushes to `main`, so there is no case it fails to cover. If `@{push}` is kept at all, gate it on *"when it resolves"* rather than *"when you have an upstream"*.

## Why this one first

Of the findings from that review, this is the one most likely to stop an agent tomorrow: it is a hard error, on the happy path, in the step that every cycle begins with.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Fixed, and the diagnosis in this issue was wrong. The cause was not a missing upstream — it was **`push.default=simple`**, which cannot resolve `@{push}` when the branch name differs from its upstream. Setting `push.default=upstream` makes `@{push}` resolve (measured: `origin/main`) and makes bare `git push` work with no `HEAD:main`. §1 still prefers `origin/main..HEAD`, which is correct under any config.

⚠ **Closed as fixed, not as "cannot recur".** The remedy here is **local git config** (and, for #88's sibling mechanics, a local repo extension) — **none of it travels with the repo**. A fresh clone gets `push.default=simple`, `pull.rebase` unset, and no `extensions.worktreeConfig`, so every one of these traps returns intact. What survives a clone is §1's *documentation* of them, which is why that text stays even though the config makes it moot in this checkout.

issues.title: AGENTS.md §1: `@{push}..HEAD` does not resolve, and the documented fallback is keyed to the wrong condition

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
From the step-4 review of the workflow change (finding 4). **Measured two ways.**

## The defect

Every line of `.gitmessage` begins with `#`, including the trailer:

```
# Co-Authored-By: Ziggy <ziggy@artificialhumanity.io>
```

Git strips comment lines from a commit message, so the template supplies the trailer visually and not actually:

```
$ git stripspace --strip-comments < .gitmessage | wc -c
0
```

and decisively — a real commit in a throwaway repo using **this repo's actual `.gitmessage`** as the template, with a subject line added, produced a message carrying **zero** `Co-Authored-By` trailers.

## Why it matters

`CLAUDE.md` mandates that trailer on commits. The template appears to supply it and silently does not, and the failure is invisible at the moment it happens — the class this repo already tracks under §5b.

**Latent, not yet realised:** every commit in the range that introduced the template carries the trailer, because those messages were written by hand rather than through it. The first commit that actually uses the template is the one that loses it.

## Fix

Un-comment the line. A template's non-comment lines are the message body, which is exactly what a trailer needs to be.

⚠ Worth a check on the fix rather than trusting it: commit through the template once and confirm the trailer survives into `git log`. The whole finding is that inspection of the file does not tell you.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Closing as fixed, on the Reviewer's argument rather than my own instinct — I was inclined to reopen it and the reasoning against that is better.

**The stated defect is repaired and checkable.** `.gitmessage`'s `Co-Authored-By` line was commented out; `git stripspace --strip-comments < .gitmessage` returned 0 bytes and now returns the trailer.

**What I found afterwards is a different fact, not this one reopened.** `commit.template` applies only to an *interactive* `git commit` — `-m` and `-F` bypass it, and every commit a session makes here uses `-F`. So the fix repairs a path nobody in this repo currently uses. That is documentation, and it landed in AGENTS.md §4 (`119a32c`, reordered in `f0235dc` so the caveat precedes the enable step).

**Nothing is actually broken:** twelve of twelve recent commits carry the trailer — this range and the last six on `main`. The only fileable version of the residual would be *"the trailer is unenforced"*, whose sole mechanism is a `commit-msg` hook carrying the identical "local config, does not travel with the repo" caveat §1 already accepts everywhere else. Not worth a tracked item.

⚠ One thing did come out of it and is fixed rather than filed: setting `commit.template` via `git config --local` wrote the **shared** config, and the path does not resolve in `/data/repos/Sonora` — which makes an interactive `git commit` **fatal** there. Now scoped with `--worktree` (`extensions.worktreeConfig` enabled), verified on both sides, and §1 carries the general property: `--local` is shared, this repo has two worktrees, check any new setting against both.

issues.title: .gitmessage: the Co-Authored-By trailer is commented out and never reaches a commit

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
From the step-4 review of the workflow change — the two gaps it found in the abort, rather than in its wording.

AGENTS.md §1's abort ("THE LOOP HAS ONE EXIT THAT IS NOT STEP 6") reads correctly and its placement is right: it names concrete triggers, refuses an automatic severity threshold for a stated reason, and closes by saying what it stands in for. Neither gap below is about that text.

## 1. No default under uncertainty, in a place where the incentive is asymmetric

Every other hard call in the file states one — §5's scope bullet ends *"when in doubt on a mixed diff, request the review."* The abort does not.

That matters because the incentive is not neutral: the worker wants to finish, and aborting means stopping and waiting for a human. An unstated default therefore resolves toward pushing, which is the direction the abort exists to prevent. One clause closes it:

> When you cannot tell whether it can live on `main`, treat it as one that cannot, and ask.

## 2. Nothing asks the REVIEW to make severity legible

The abort is the **worker's** action, but the judgement originates in the **review**. §1 specifies what the worker's brief must contain; no bullet specifies what the review must contain.

The cycle that produced this finding only worked because the brief happened to ask the reviewer to mark must-fix-before-push explicitly — and the reviewer did, opening its report with `⚠ MUST-FIX-BEFORE-PUSH: NONE`. That was an ad-hoc instance, not a rule. The next worker may not think to ask, and then the abort has no input.

Worth one line in §1: **the review must state, per finding, whether it is must-fix-before-push.**

## Note on scope

This is the interim loop, which the owner is replacing. Both gaps are properties of the *actor–critic handoff* rather than of this particular spelling of it, so they are worth carrying into whatever replaces it: a critic that does not grade severity leaves the actor to invent the grade, and an actor with no stated default under uncertainty will pick the one that lets it finish.
issues.title: The abort has no default under uncertainty, and nothing requires a review to mark severity

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
Raised in the step-4 review and re-measured here (git 2.53.0, throwaway repos, diverged state printed before every run). This is the highest-consequence gap in the interim loop, because every step of it is a *conforming* action and the failure is silent.

## The chain

1. §1 says push directly; if `main` moved, the push is rejected. git's rejection hints: *"Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally… integrate the remote changes (e.g. `git pull …`)"*.
2. A worker follows that hint. **`git pull` is fatal on diverged branches when `pull.rebase` is unset**, which is this repo's state at *every* config scope (`local`, `global`, `system`, `worktree` — all verified unset):

```
hint:   git config pull.rebase false  # merge
hint:   git config pull.rebase true   # rebase
hint:   git config pull.ff only       # fast-forward only
fatal: Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches.
```

3. The three remedies look equal. A worker that picks the second sets **`pull.rebase true` permanently**.
4. From then on every integration rebases, which rewrites the local commits — so the reviewed SHAs cease to exist, the `notes/reviews/review-<sha7>.md` handoff is orphaned, and §1's own rule ("if you rebase, the reviewed range is gone and the cycle is over") fires **every cycle, with no signal**.

§1 already says *merge, not rebase*. What it does not do is name a command, so the worker gets the command from git — and git offers the trap as one of three peers.

## Measured, all three forms, same diverged state

Each row is a fresh clone, made genuinely diverged (local ahead 1, remote ahead 1 — `git rev-list --left-right --count` printed as `1/1` before each run), `pull.rebase` confirmed UNSET:

| form | result |
|---|---|
| `git pull` | **fatal**, exit 128 — *Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches* |
| `git pull origin main` | **fatal**, exit 128 — identical |
| `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` | exit 0, *Merge made by the 'ort' strategy* |

⚠ **There is no safe explicit form of `git pull` here.** The reconciliation strategy is chosen when pull decides merge-vs-rebase, which happens regardless of how the refspec was supplied.

## Fix

* **Name the command in §1**: after a rejected push, **`git fetch origin && git merge origin/main`**. It is unambiguous, it cannot rebase, it needs no config, and it is the one form measured working.
* **Consider setting `pull.rebase false`** — ⚠ but note the blast radius before doing it. `extensions.worktreeConfig` is unset here, so `git config --local` writes the **shared** config and would change `git pull` behaviour for every worktree of this repo, including `/data/repos/Sonora`, which another session uses. That makes it an owner decision rather than a worker's.

## Why it belongs in the tracker rather than a doc tweak

The interim loop is being replaced, but this is not a property of the loop — it is a property of *any* workflow that pushes to a shared branch and cares about commit identity. A critic keyed to SHAs and a VCS whose default hint rewrites SHAs will collide in whatever comes next.

---

⚠ **Correction, recorded because the error is more instructive than the finding.** An earlier version of this issue claimed the fatal was specific to the *bare* form, and recommended `git pull origin main` as the way through — which walks the reader into the same fatal and the same three hints. That claim came from a test whose instrument was contaminated: it passed `git -c pull.rebase= pull …`, which **sets `pull.rebase` to the empty string rather than leaving it unset**, and an empty value reconciles as merge. The test configured the very variable whose absence it was checking, then reported the resulting merge as evidence that the form was safe. Re-run without the flag and with the ahead/behind count printed first, all three rows above came out as shown.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Fixed at the source. `pull.rebase=false` is set, so the fatal never fires and the hint that offers `pull.rebase true` is never shown. Measured on a genuinely diverged pair (ahead/behind printed as 1/1): bare `git pull` exits 0, *Merge made by the 'ort' strategy*, and the local commit survives **as a parent** — so reviewed SHAs are preserved, which was the whole point.

⚠ **Closed as fixed, not as "cannot recur".** The remedy here is **local git config** (and, for #88's sibling mechanics, a local repo extension) — **none of it travels with the repo**. A fresh clone gets `push.default=simple`, `pull.rebase` unset, and no `extensions.worktreeConfig`, so every one of these traps returns intact. What survives a clone is §1's *documentation* of them, which is why that text stays even though the config makes it moot in this checkout.

issues.title: AGENTS.md §1: git's own hint steers a worker into `pull.rebase true`, which silently ends every future review cycle

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
Raised in the step-4 review of the workflow change, and demonstrated in the same cycle it was raised in.

## The gap

AGENTS.md §1 caps the loop hard: one fix pass, one re-review, then file and push — *"a third lap is never correct, however tempting the findings."* That cap is deliberate and it is the only mechanism the loop has.

But it does not distinguish two different things:

* **a third lap on the same range** — the loop the cap exists to prevent;
* **new commits arriving after the review** — which are not a lap at all.

Because the doc does not draw that line, a worker holding freshly-arrived commits reads the cap as covering them, and **pushing them unread becomes the conforming behaviour** rather than a lapse. There is no rule being broken.

## It is not hypothetical

In the cycle that introduced these rules, `e75308c` and `5f7e62e` both landed after the review report and both reached `main` unreviewed. Both came from owner instructions arriving mid-cycle.

⚠ **This is the case the range-not-commit fix cannot cover.** That fix stopped the range growing because the *worker* kept committing; it cannot stop the range growing because the *owner* said something new. Every cycle so far has had the range move after the brief, and the causes are now two distinct ones.

## Fix

One sentence naming the distinction:

> A third lap on the same range is what the cap forbids. **Commits that arrive after the review are a new cycle, not a lap** — they get their own review before they are pushed.

That makes the honest cost visible too: if new work keeps arriving, the loop does not converge, and the right move is to stop taking new work into the cycle rather than to keep pushing unread commits.

## Also, a number to re-derive

§1 currently reads *"Measured on this loop's first three cycles: the range grew after the brief every time."* It is now four, and the count moved **twice inside a single cycle** while that sentence sat unchanged. Re-derive rather than increment — the same failure mode §5b names, in a sentence about measurement.

## Scope note

Like #85, this is a property of the actor–critic handoff rather than of this spelling of it: any loop with a bounded number of critic passes needs a rule for work that arrives while the critic is reading. Worth carrying into whatever replaces the interim loop.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
**Half done — narrowing rather than closing**, on the step-4 re-review's read.

**Landed:** §1 now states the distinction this issue asked for — *commits that arrive after the review are a new cycle, not a third lap* — and the cycle-count sentence was re-derived rather than incremented.

⚠ **What is still missing is the consequence, which is what this issue was actually about.** Classification alone does not stop the shipping:

> **A push carries every unpushed commit.** Calling late commits "a new cycle" does not prevent them going out — the worker still arrives at step 6 with them in the range. *Correct classification* and *unreviewed shipping* are fully compatible under the current text.

That is exactly what happened to `e75308c` and `5f7e62e`: both were correctly understood as new work, and both reached `main` unreviewed anyway.

**The missing rule is sequencing, not vocabulary:**

> Do not push until every unpushed commit has been through a completed cycle. **The unit that must be reviewed is the push, not the cycle.**

Retitling scope accordingly: the ask is now the sequencing rule, and the naming distinction is done.

issues.title: The loop cannot absorb commits that arrive mid-cycle, and pushing them unread is the conforming behaviour

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
Measured on the second cycle of the interim loop. Filed because the cost is not hypothetical — it already happened, and only an accident prevented it from being invisible.

## What happened

AGENTS.md §1 says the reviewer writes its report to `notes/reviews/review-<sha7>.md`, and step 6 says the worker deletes it at the end of the cycle. **Neither says when the file is finished**, and a file that is being written is indistinguishable on disk from a file that is done.

So:

1. The Reviewer wrote a first version of `review-bc1d81d.md`.
2. The worker read it, acted on it, closed the cycle, and deleted it (verified: `rm -f` on both files, `ls` returned `README.md` alone).
3. The Reviewer was **mid-rewrite** — a second version, renumbered `A–H`, incorporating findings about commits that arrived after the first brief. That Write landed at `15:52:49`, seven minutes after the cycle closed and after the deletion.

The file's existence on disk had been taken as the completion signal. It was not one.

## The cost, which is what settles it

**Everything in the second version was deleted unread** — including the `git pull` trap and the mid-cycle-commits finding.

⚠ **#86 and #87 exist only because the Reviewer also put those findings in a `SendMessage`**, which the protocol does not ask for anywhere. Had §1 been followed literally, with the file treated as the handoff, the two highest-ranked findings of that cycle would have been silently lost and neither party would have known anything was missing. The duplication that saved them was accidental.

That is the repo's signature failure — an instrument that reports nothing, indistinguishable from an instrument that reports all-clear.

## Fix

One sentence:

> **A review is delivered when the `Reviewer` says so, not when the file appears.** The file is the content; the message is the completion event. Do not read, act on, or delete a `review-*.md` before the Reviewer has said it is complete.

## It also dissolves an existing awkwardness

If the message is the handoff and the file is its attachment, then "which SHA names the file" (currently pinned to the tip of the range at request time, to stop two agents choosing differently) stops carrying weight, and step 6 simply deletes whatever the cycle produced once the Reviewer has confirmed it is done. See #82, which is already about the loop being stated in two places — the completion rule belongs wherever that lands.

## Scope note

Like #85 and #87, this is a property of the actor–critic handoff rather than of this spelling of it: **any** design where the critic's output is a file rather than an event has this race, and the fix is the same — the artifact needs a completion signal that is not its own existence.

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Fixed. AGENTS.md §1 now carries the rule: **a review is delivered when the `Reviewer` says so, not when the file appears.** The file is the content; the message is the completion event. Both cycles since have used it — the reviewer opens with an explicit *REPORT IS COMPLETE* line and I do not read or delete the file before it.

⚠ **Closed as fixed, not as "cannot recur".** The remedy here is **local git config** (and, for #88's sibling mechanics, a local repo extension) — **none of it travels with the repo**. A fresh clone gets `push.default=simple`, `pull.rebase` unset, and no `extensions.worktreeConfig`, so every one of these traps returns intact. What survives a clone is §1's *documentation* of them, which is why that text stays even though the config makes it moot in this checkout.

issues.title: Nothing marks a review as complete, so a partially-written report was deleted unread

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
From the step-4 re-review of the streamlining change. Re-measured here before filing.

## The trap

§4 tells the reader to enable the commit template with `git config --worktree commit.template .gitmessage`, carrying a ⚠ that says **`--worktree`, not `--local`** — because `--local` writes the shared config and a template path that does not resolve makes an interactive `git commit` *fatal* in another worktree.

⚠ **`--worktree` IS `--local` unless `extensions.worktreeConfig` is enabled.** Measured, both directions:

| extension | `git config --worktree probe.key …` writes | exit | warning |
|---|---|---|---|
| **off** | `.git/config` — the **shared** config | 0 | none, and no `config.worktree` is created |
| on | `.git/config.worktree` | 0 | — |

So a reader in a fresh clone follows the instruction *including its warning*, silently writes the shared config, and can reproduce the exact fatal-commit breakage the warning exists to prevent.

**`extensions.worktreeConfig` is itself local config and does not travel** — which §4 says about the template four lines further down, about a different setting. A fresh clone has the extension off by default.

## Fix

State the precondition, and give a falsifier rather than an assurance:

* enable `extensions.worktreeConfig` first, and
* verify with **`git config --show-origin --get <key>`** — **the origin must be a `config.worktree` path, not `.git/config`.**

Here that currently reads `file:/data/repos/Sonora/.git/worktrees/lab-manager/config.worktree`, which is what correct looks like.

## Three smaller things in the same text

* **§1's shared-config bullet is half-actionable.** *"Use `--worktree` for anything that names a path"* is concrete; *"check any new setting against both checkouts"* names no method — and the obvious instrument is one already measured as broken, since `git commit --dry-run` does **not** read the template. Name it: `git -C /data/repos/Sonora config --get <key>`, and for a path-valued setting confirm the path exists there.
* **That bullet is in the wrong place.** It sits under *"One session commits to this repo"*, but the hazard comes from the repo having **two worktrees**, and single-committer reasoning is precisely what masked it. Its own second sentence rebuts the premise of the bullet it lives inside.
* **§4 still says "⚠ Local config,"** about a setting it has just told the reader to set with `--worktree`, three lines after making `--local` the thing to avoid. Stale word, and the continuation lines are mis-indented.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed

It arrived in the step-4 re-review, after the cycle's one fix pass — so per AGENTS.md §1 it becomes an issue. The reviewer marked it **not** must-fix-before-push: the trap is inert in this checkout, where the extension is on and verified.
issues.title: AGENTS.md's `--worktree, not --local` instruction silently writes shared config in a fresh clone

issues.author: lmcfarlin
issues.body:
Found 2026-08-11 while auditing the direction pipeline against a set of externally-proposed "Director→Matcha conditioning" guidelines. Not from a PR review, and no code has been changed.

## The claim

Synthesis QC is designed as two stages, and only stage 1 runs.

`scripts/synthesis/qc_gate.py:25-27`, its own header:

> Verdict merge (intended-vs-measured label check, keeps list, owner audit sample) is qc_verdict.py's job once EIV scores exist — this script only measures and hard-gates.

`scripts/synthesis/synth_bank.sh:241` names stage 2 in a comment and never invokes it:

> The gate is stage 1 only (measures + hard gates); qc_verdict.py still owns the intended-vs-measured merge.

Stage 1 already writes the handoff: `qc_gate.py` emits `<campaign>/qc_filelist.txt` explicitly "for scripts/eiv_score.py". It has been producing the input to a stage that does not run.

The consequence is that the gate which "FOLLOWS EVERY dataset-generation pass" (owner rule 2026-07-31, quoted in `synth_bank.sh`) is nine hard checks and all nine are intrinsic audio quality — nonempty, internal pause, duration-vs-text, ASR WER, tail loss, clip length, speech ≥ 4 s, DNSMOS, measures-computable. Not one of them reads `intended{V,A,T}`, which sits unused in the same manifest row.

## Measured scope

Across `/data/model-training/datasets`, 14 campaigns have `qc_measures.jsonl` and 4 have `qc_verdicts.jsonl`.

**Correctly excluded:** the librivox campaigns are real audio and carry **zero** `intended` labels — `librivox-v1` (664 clips), `librivox-v2` (1,366), `librivox-speech-v1` (79, plus a 79-clip precut). There is nothing to verify against and their lack of verdicts is not a defect.

**Affected** — synthetic clips carrying `intended` labels for which no verdict was ever produced:

| campaign | clips | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `delivery-v1-narration` | 360 | 2026-08-01 |
| `delivery-v1-narration-r2` | 142 | 2026-08-04 |
| `teacher-ab-v1` | 80 | 2026-07-26 |
| `newscaster-v1` | 78 | 2026-08-02 |
| `sonora-expressive-registers/quote-pilot-v3d` | 35 | 2026-07-23 |
| **total** | **695** | |

The four campaigns that do have verdicts are the three `synthetic_v1/*` campaigns `qc_verdict` was written for (2026-07-17/19) plus `revisit-v1` (2026-07-28). Nothing since. Note that `teacher-ab-v1` and `quote-pilot-v3d` both predate `revisit-v1`, so this was intermittent before it stopped entirely — it was never systematic.

## How much the check would have caught

From the last campaign that ran it, `synthetic_v1/bulk1`:

| | count |
|---|---|
| clips | 159 |
| passed the intrinsic hard gates | 148 |
| became keeps | 69 |
| **intrinsically clean but failed ≥ 1 axis** | **79 (53.4% of 148)** |

Axis failures among those 148: **V 41 · T 31 · A 28**.

Recomputed from `bulk1/qc_verdicts.jsonl` for this issue and restricted to `hard_pass` clips, since that is the population the missing stage would act on.

## Why this is a defect rather than a design choice

The same failure mode has been diagnosed and fixed twice in `synth_bank.sh`, and both fixes are commented in place:

- on `qc_gate` itself — *"This step used to be manual, and nothing here invoked it — so every batch reached the audition queue ungated unless somebody remembered."*
- on `qc_engine_defects` — *"This was a MANUAL step until 2026-08-08, which made it a coverage hole rather than an instrument… a detector nobody runs trades nothing."*

`qc_verdict` is the third instance of the identical pattern, and the one still outstanding.

Nothing blocks it. All four of `qc_verdict.py`'s hardcoded anchors resolve on disk, and they are deliberately fixed reference scales ("the same LibriTTS-anchored z-scales the Emilia mining used"), not stale paths. `scripts/eiv_score.sh` exists as a throwaway-container runner, is resumable, and its header states that the training spin-down rule does not apply to a labelling pass. That wrapper landed 2026-08-01 — three days after the last verdict was ever produced.

## What it actually costs

**Not a mislabelled corpus.** Corpus labels are re-measured from the rendered audio (`measure_expressive_registers.py`, `derive_vat_corpus.py`), so a clip directed angry that renders calm enters the corpus *labelled calm*. Label correctness is protected by a different mechanism, and that protection is real.

The costs are:

**1. `gate_calibration.py` is starved, irreversibly, one campaign at a time.** Its constraint:

> Every full-coverage round is a free opportunity to measure it, but only if the instrument verdicts are frozen BEFORE the owner rates. Afterwards there is nothing to compare against and the round is spent.

Dataset pipeline 1.0 — the owner spot-checking instead of auditing every clip — is gated on exactly that measurement. Every un-verdicted campaign has spent the opportunity permanently. This is the expensive part, and it is why the issue is not simply "some clips went unchecked."

**2. Silent distributional drift.** Nothing reports that a direction failed, so the corpus drifts toward whatever the engines actually do rather than toward what was asked for. The `bulk1` table above is the only estimate we have of the size of that effect.

**3. It fails quietly at both ends.** `audit_sampler.py:112-114` skips any book with no `qc_verdicts.jsonl` after a one-line warning, and `synth_bank.sh` prints `QC-GATE-DONE` on the intrinsic pass alone — which reads as "this batch is good" while the direction axis has been examined by nothing.

## The fix is NOT a copy of the qc_gate wiring

`keep` in `qc_verdict` is a **label-confirmation** gate, not a quality gate. `gate_calibration.py:24-30`:

> A beautiful clip whose director-assigned labels were wrong is a legitimate not-keep. So a large instrument-rejects/ear-keeps cell may indict the DIRECTOR's labels rather than the engine or the instrument — check which before concluding anything.

Wiring it fail-closed like `qc_gate` would discard good audio because Gemma mislabelled it. It belongs on the `qc_engine_defects` pattern instead: always runs, writes verdicts, appends to `qc_flags.txt`, never drops a clip.

## Proposed shape

1. After `qc_gate` and **before** `register_audition`, run `eiv_score.sh` over `$CAMPAIGN_DIR/qc_filelist.txt`.
2. Run `qc_verdict.py --eiv …`, writing `qc_verdicts.jsonl` **frozen before the ear sees anything**. The ordering is what makes the round usable by `gate_calibration`, and it is the part most easily got wrong.
3. Append axis failures to `qc_flags.txt` so `pick_audit_subset --flags` routes them to the ear — the QC-flag path never relaxes by tier.
4. Non-fatal and announced on failure, exactly like `qc_engine_defects`.
5. Skip cleanly when a campaign carries no `intended` labels, so real-audio banks are a no-op rather than an error.

## Read before trusting it

- **`qc_verdict.py` has not been modified since 2026-07-18** (`ad2fa56`). It predates the loudness correction (07-28), the delivery channel shipping (08-07) and Documentary's retirement (08-10). It checks V/A/T axes only, which is correct — delivery is not an axis it could check — but the code deserves a read against contract v2 rather than merely being invoked.
- **Its A is not the corpus's A.** `qc_verdict.raw_measures` takes arousal from the EIV Arousal head, while the LibriTTS corpus lane derives A as a per-speaker LUFS z-score. The divergence is deliberate and documented in `normalize_loudness.py`, but it means a clip can satisfy one definition of A and fail the other. The verdict output should state which it used.
- **Backfill is a diagnostic, not a calibration.** The 695 clips and their manifests still exist, so verdicts can be produced retroactively — but they would be produced *after* the ear rated them, so they cannot serve `gate_calibration`. Backfill would measure the drift; it cannot recover the spent rounds.

## What this issue wants

Stage 2 wired on the advisory pattern, before Phase 1S opens. Both existing plans already require it, and neither can proceed without it:

- `notes/quality-gap-plan.md` § Phase 1S, prerequisite 3 — *"Every synthetic clip already carries **both** Gemma's `intended` V/A/T (in the manifest) and the acoustically-measured V/A/T derived from the render. **Nothing compares them.**"*
- `notes/direction-contract-v3-proposal.md` §4, rule 4 — *"Rule 4 is the one that does not exist yet and matters most for Phase 1S. Mass synthesis without an automatic direction-following score is mass production of unverified labels."*

comments.author: lmcfarlin
comments.body:
Classified in #26: this is one instance of a class. `scripts/` holds 112 non-test files and 27 of them are invoked by nothing — almost all correctly, since they are finished campaign tooling. So "nothing calls this file" is the normal state there and carries no signal, which is why `qc_verdict` was indistinguishable from a retired one-shot sitting in the same directory as its caller.

#26 proposes the coverage test that would have caught it: declare the stages a dataset-generation pass must run, and assert the orchestrator invokes each — the same technique `matcha/direction.py` already uses for conditioning channels.

One finding from that pass belongs here directly: **a text search reports this issue's defect as already fixed.** The string `qc_verdict.py` does appear in `synth_bank.sh`, at line 241, inside a comment. Restricting to non-comment lines is what exposes it, so the test in #26 has to parse invocations rather than grep for filenames.
